New legislation giving priority to UK medical graduates seeking NHS training posts has had a dramatic impact on boosting the number of homegrown doctors, figures suggest.

An analysis of NHS data by the Nuffield Trust think tank found that legal changes in March achieved their aim of prioritising doctors trained in the NHS over those who trained overseas.

The changes were introduced by Wes Streeting when he was health secretary, who said he wanted to "put homegrown talent at the front of the queue for medical training posts".

Trainee doctors have long argued that far too many candidates are competing for a small pool of available places.

In the decade to 2025, the total number of specialty training applications increased more than five-fold from about 16,500 to almost 85,000 a year, driven mainly by overseas medics.

The new data shows that 28% of doctors accepting a specialty training place (the stage before becoming a GP or consultant) in 2025 were from what is now defined as the “non-priority” group, which includes most doctors who trained overseas.

Trainees have long said there are far too many of them chasing a small number of places ( PA )

After the change to prioritise UK graduates in March, this figure fell to 1.8%.

The proportion of doctors accepting NHS specialty training places from the group that includes most overseas-trained doctors has now fallen from more than one in four to fewer than one in 50.

Overall, there were 6,734 acceptances from the priority group (the vast majority of whom trained in the UK) out of 9,351 in 2025.

In 2026, the proportion has risen dramatically so that 9,122 out of 9,286 acceptances are from doctors largely trained in the UK.

Nuffield Trust fellow, Lucina Rolewicz, said: “There is no doubt that the new law has had a big impact in terms of strengthening the domestic training pipeline for doctors.

“The numbers show just how dramatically the rules introduced this year have shifted access to specialty training away from overseas-trained doctors and towards predominantly UK-trained doctors.

“The question now is what this means for the NHS in the longer term.

“The NHS needs to make sure that prioritising homegrown doctors boosts the domestic workforce without reducing the overall supply of doctors and creating concerning staffing gaps.”

The think tank said that in the future, specialties that have historically relied more heavily on overseas graduates could be affected by shortages, including general practice, psychiatry and obstetrics.

The priority group includes NHS-trained doctors and medics who trained in countries where the UK has longstanding reciprocal agreements, including Ireland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

The Department of Health and the British Medical Association (BMA) have been approached for comment.

News.title: Bank of England must raise interest rates, says chief economist
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Government borrowing costs edged lower on Thursday as Andy Burnham continues to face scrutiny over the public finances.

The yield on 10-year US treasury bonds – considered a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money – declined slightly to 4.78pc on Thursday after a drop in oil prices.

Pre-market trading of bonds in Britain, France and Germany suggested the market was poised to rally after a brutal first half of the week.

However, Mr Burnham and Chancellor John Healey remain under intense pressure, with analysts estimating that as much as half of the country’s fiscal headroom has been wiped out by the jump in bond yields.

Borrowing costs surged after a jump in oil prices caused by fresh strikes between the US and Iran.

The yield on 10-year gilts, as UK bonds are known, hit levels not seen since the global financial crisis in 2007, while longer-term debt costs hit their highest point since 1998.

It means the Chancellor will have less room for manoeuvre in the Budget next month, with some economists predicting the rise in borrowing costs has wiped out up to £14bn of breathing room.

The rise in bond yields across major economies had deepened concerns about deteriorating financial conditions.

Central banks in the US and Europe are increasingly expected to raise interest rates this month to combat inflation caused by the Iran war, although the Bank of England is expected to hold rates steady for now.

Gavin Friend, an analyst at NAB, said: “If this war ‌were to be ‌put to bed, then that ⁠would certainly be something very positive to bring yields back down again across the board.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Oil prices slipped, helping boost stocks and bonds.

Renewed fighting between the US and Iran pushed oil prices sharply higher earlier in the week.

However, Brent crude was trading near $94 a barrel after Donald Trump said he does not expect the US bombing campaign to last “much longer”.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 advanced 0.2pc to 64,455.83. Among major gainers, OpenAI investor SoftBank Group rose 2.9pc, memory chipmaker Kioxia rose 0.6pc, and chip equipment manufacturer Tokyo Electron gained 0.8pc.

South Korea’s Kospi rose 1.4pc to 6,656.81. Samsung was 1.3pc higher, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix was up 1.4pc.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng edged 0.1pc higher, to 25,344.80. The Shanghai Composite index climbed 0.4pc to 3,958.79.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.5pc to 9,025.10.

The Taiex in Taiwan rose 0.6pc, while India’s Sensex climbed 0.3pc.

It comes after Wall Street bounced back after its sharp sell-off at the start of September, as investors snapped up shares that had fallen in recent days.

The S&P 500 rose, with almost 350 companies ending higher. Dell was among the biggest winners, jumping 14pc after giving an upbeat outlook, while investors were also looking ahead to results from chipmaker Broadcom.

The recovery came despite continued concerns over inflation, with oil prices remaining high as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude briefly climbed close to $97 a barrel before easing back after Donald Trump said he did not expect the renewed bombing campaign to last “too long”.

US government bond yields were little changed after surging to their highest levels in several years earlier in the week.

Investors also got a mixed picture from the Federal Reserve’s latest assessment of the US economy. Economic activity increased modestly over the past two months, helped by strong demand from data centres, while companies added jobs at a slower pace in August.

The figures come ahead of Friday’s closely watched US jobs report, which could influence expectations for the next move in interest rates.

News.title: Weapons and mercenaries from foreign states fuelling Sudan’s war, UN report finds
News.content:
The war in Sudan is being fuelled by weapons and mercenaries from external states including the United Arab Emirates, Colombia and Turkey, a United Nations report has found.

An investigation by a UN fact-finding mission published on Thursday found that the supply of drones in particular to both sides in the civil war was extending the fighting’s reach and contributing to war crimes.

“Increasingly sophisticated drone capabilities [has] enabled both parties to strike far beyond immediate front lines”, says the report.

“The [UN] mission calls on States to enforce the Darfur arms embargo and suspend transfers of weapons, drones, components, or military assistance where there is a substantial risk of their use in serious violations”.

Sudan’s civil war erupted in April 2023 following a power struggle between the head of the military and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as part of a planned transition to civilian rule. Hundreds of thousands have died and some 14 million people have been displaced in what has become the world’s deadliest conflict.

In a previous report in February, following the capture of El Fasher in which at least 60,000 people were killed, the UN said the RSF’s mass killings of Black African ethnic groups, including Zaghawa and Fur, bore the “hallmarks of genocide”.

The latest report said “individuals and entities” in the UAE were part of a transnational network supplying weapons, logistics, training and foreign personnel to the RSF – including NORINCO AH-4 howitzers, FK-20000 air defence systems and Chinese-made CH-95 strike drones.

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), meanwhile, separately obtained Turkish-manufactured drones, including Bayraktar Akıncı combat drones and Yiha III loitering munitions.

The Turkish embassy in London has been contacted for comment.

News.title: The Ukrainian children struggling to survive alone in Europe
News.content:
Every day begins and ends in the same way for Arsenii, 17: calling his mum back home in Kyiv. A year ago he moved from Ukraine to a school boarding house in Slovakia. One night he fell asleep before phoning. When he woke, his mobile was flooded with messages from the few adults his mum knew in the country: the dorm security guard and agent she paid to become his temporary legal guardian. “She woke up everybody,” he says, still with a sense of guilt. She had been trying, agonisingly, to account for her son from over 1,000km away.

Russia’s unprovoked full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 triggered Europe’s largest displacement of children since World War II. More than 1.8 million crossed into neighbouring countries in the first month – 90 per cent of them with their mothers or other female relatives. But as bombardments battered the country in the following four years, children continued to leave – only without their relatives.

A year-long investigation by the Telegraph has discovered thousands of Ukrainian children are living in Europe alone in the hope of a better life. Some have adapted to independent living, studying and learning the local language. Others have fallen into illegal work, experienced insecurity and discrimination. A few attempts end in tragedy.

The exact number of Ukrainian children who are now living alone in Europe is unclear. Data collected by EU statistical database Eurostat suggests the total cases since 2022 could be almost 23,500. It shows that 19,580 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors in European Union (EU) countries received EU Temporary Protection Status (TPS) between March 2022 and July 2026.

Non-EU countries offer parallel protection schemes. Eurostat data revealed that in the same time-frame, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland granted their protection status to an additional 3,905 unaccompanied Ukrainian minors.

However, the data is incomplete. Only 20 out of 27 EU members declared their numbers. Among those missing are key Ukrainian refugee destination countries, such as Germany and Poland. Poland alone issued 42,332 temporary guardian orders to Ukrainian minors between 2022 and 2025, according to Polish Ministry of Justice data requested by The Telegraph.

In theory, any child granted TPS protection should have a locally appointed legal guardian to sign their papers. However, our investigation revealed loopholes in the system, leaving this category of children vulnerable to abandonment or poor guardianship arrangements.

Arsenii is among at least 1,024 Ukrainian children aged 14 to 16 who have evacuated to Slovak school boarding houses, according to a snapshot 2025 survey by the Slovak Children’s Commissioner. The real figure is likely to be thousands higher, as this research covered just over half of secondary schools in five of the country’s eight regions. It concluded some 5,000 Ukrainian minors in Slovakia have no responsible adult “close to them”, of whom around 1,000 have no legal representative at all.

News.title: Zika virus mosquitoes breed in Britain for first time
News.content:
The UK has historically been too cold for the tropical mosquitoes to survive, but they have been slowly making their way up through Europe.

As temperatures warm, it is predicted that the mosquitoes could become widespread, potentially bringing with them diseases associated with Africa and the tropics.

“The timing of this detection is particularly interesting because the UK has just experienced its provisionally hottest summer on record,” Dr César López-Camacho, a researcher at the University of Oxford, said.



“Warmer conditions can accelerate mosquito development, extend the period in which mosquitoes remain active and, critically, increase the rate at which viruses such as dengue or chikungunya replicate within a competent mosquito,” Dr López-Camacho added.

Previous government modelling suggested that the mosquitoes would be unlikely to get a foothold in Britain until 2040, but the new discovery of the colony in London suggests it may happen sooner.

It means diseases such as dengue fever – which causes high fevers and severe joint pain, and can be fatal, particularly in the elderly and young children – could become common in southern England.

News.title: Burnham risks Truss moment, warn bond traders
News.content:
Andy Burnham risks a Liz Truss-style market meltdown unless he presents a credible plan to pay for his agenda, bond traders have warned.

Investors said the Prime Minister faces further spikes in borrowing costs unless he outlines tax rises or spending cuts to fund his major policies.

UK borrowing costs have surged to multi-decade highs this week amid a global bond market sell-off. However, investors are particularly concerned about Mr Burnham’s fiscal agenda before his first Budget next month.

Al Cattermole, a portfolio manager at Swiss private bank Mirabaud, said investors were “unclear” about the Prime Minister’s plans and how he would pay for them.

He said: “If you have a lack of credibility about your spending plan and how that will be funded, then you would get spikes in yields similar to [what] we saw during the Liz Truss episode.

“That was about unfunded fiscal spending. And if you get that again, then there is concern about that.”

Mr Burnham refused to rule out increasing borrowing during his first Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday despite recent market turmoil.

Jim Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment, said: “Spending cuts are the thing the market wants to hear.

“It would go a long way if this Government were to recognise that it is a challenge that needs addressing – that the path we are on in terms of welfare spending is completely unsustainable.”

He added: “The market knows that, and the market wants to hear that the Government understands that.”

Lord Jim O’Neill said earlier that the Prime Minister must “get real” and cut public spending in order to ease pressure in the bond market.

The cost of long-term government borrowing hit its highest level since 1998 on Wednesday, increasing the strain on the public finances as John Healey, the new Chancellor, prepares for the Budget.

The 10-year gilt yield – a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money – has risen to its highest point since 2007.

News.title: H5N1 hits US mink farms, sparking calls for an urgent cull
News.content:
H5N1 has been detected on a US mink farm for the first time, igniting fears the infected animals could present a human pandemic risk.

The bird flu virus, which has “jumped” from birds to numerous mammal species and infected hundreds of people in recent years, was detected in at least six mink on a farm in Utah in mid-August, according to a notification from the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) released over the weekend.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms gives invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate. Mink also have strikingly similar respiratory systems to humans, which greatly increases the human risk.

The animals are farmed for their fur, which is then typically exported to fashion manufacturers in China, Hong Kong, and Russia and used in items like coats and scarves.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 acquires the ability to spread efficiently between people, it could trigger a human pandemic.

“Avian influenza viruses tend to replicate pretty poorly in humans and don’t really have the right sort of properties that allow them to transmit from person to person.

“If H5N1 were to cause a pandemic, it would need to make quite a lot of changes, and there’s a real concern that mink, particularly farmed mink, have a lot of the features that could drive the evolution of H5N1,” Dr Tom Peacock, a virologist at The Pirbright Institute, told The Telegraph.

News.title: Collapsing child vaccination in South Africa ‘a public health emergency’
News.content:
Plummeting child immunisation rates are now a public health emergency in South Africa and risk causing outbreaks of preventable but potentially deadly childhood diseases, the government has said.

The proportion of children under one who have received no vaccinations has trebled in the past decade to nearly a third of infants in South Africa.

Mistrust of vaccines and growing ignorance about the benefits of childhood immunisations risk undoing years of progress made by one of the continent’s most effective health systems.

Outbreaks of measles, diphtheria and whooping cough this year have all been linked to poor immunisation rates and are evidence that herd immunity is breaking down, officials warned.

An alert from the department for health said the proportion of unvaccinated infants had hit 36.3 per cent in the first four months of 2026, up from 12.1 per cent in 2017.

The department warned the jump was “effectively tripling the number of completely unvaccinated children and leaving hundreds of thousands of infants at risk of life-threatening illnesses”.

Coverage of the six-in-one hexavalent infant vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, meningitis, and hepatitis B declined from 87 per cent to 60.5 per cent over the same period.

Officials said the shortfall was caused by a lack of people coming forward to bring their children for jabs and was not due to any shortage of vaccines.

Dr Nonhlanhla Ndlovu, deputy director general of South Africa’s health department, told the state broadcaster that parents had a poor understanding of the public health benefits of childhood jabs.

She said: “The second one that comes out is the issue of public trust, in terms of the safety of the vaccines, but also the trust in terms of our systems.”

“Theses vaccines are very safe and we have seen the gains that we have had in our years before and now that is changing.

“The benefit of vaccines far outweigh anything we can talk about in public health. We need them to come back and bring the children for immunisation.”

Sports.title: Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate
Sports.content:
Mike Dean 'nonsense' claims rubbished by former referees as FA urged to investigate

Controversial retired official Mike Dean's comments about his time as a Premier League referee has led to a strong reaction from two former top-flight officials

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Two former Premier League referees have criticised Mike Dean after the ex-official claimed to have played secret ‘games’ in matches during his time in the top flight. The former referee claimed that such games would involve waiting to see how long he could go without blowing the whistle or leaving the centre circle.

‌



Dean spent more than two decades as a referee in English football before retiring from the profession in 2022, and went on to spend a further year as a video assistant referee.

‌



During an appearance on Jamie Vardy's Having a Party podcast, Dean said: "There used to be games that we used to have, as a laugh, we used to say, 'Right, we'll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle.'

‌



"Done that a few times in the Premier, before VAR obviously. Went 20–25 minutes without blowing a whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.

Ismaila Sarr dream transfer amid Liverpool interest as stance perfectly clear READ MORE :

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. The lads used to be on the line saying 'you can't'. I said 'I'll try it'. I just used to run around but don't come out of it. Got about 15 minutes once in one game, without leaving the centre circle."

Such comments have caused some outrage among the football community with calls for the FA to launch an investigation, while two former referees have openly criticised Dean as a result.

‌



Former Premier League referee Graham Scott labelled the claims from Dean about games within matches as ‘nonsense’.

“I worked with Mike [Dean] loads at times, they’re not true stories,” Scott told talkSPORT.

“It’s kind of the audio equivalent of clickbait isn’t it, to try and get people interested and laughing. It’s palpable nonsense.

‌



“Mike Dean [was] of course an outstanding ref, but it makes it so much harder when retired referees either bash their former colleagues for the sake of it.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It’s fine to criticise, I do that, but do it with a bit of context and a bit of empathy.”

Scott later added: “I challenge Mike and say, ‘Okay, would you stand in front of the current refs and repeat all of those things?’

“And of course he wouldn’t, because they’re not true.”

‌



Mark Halsey, another former Premier League referee, was in disbelief at the comments made by Dean.

“All my years as a professional referee, I have to say I’ve never heard of these games. Never,” Halsey told BBC Sport.

View 2 Images Mike Dean (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

‌

“Because they’re massive games, you’ve got the fans, you’ve got the players, you’ve got the managers, the delegates, the coaches.

“So I’m astounded, and if Mike has played these games, then he’s done that on his own accord.

Sports.title: Man Utd loan out Chido Obi as youngster risks following concerning Old Trafford pattern
Sports.content:
When it comes to Manchester United youngsters breaking through and lasting the course, Kobbie Mainoo is perhaps the one shining example.

For the majority though they follow similar patterns. A bit of fanfare and hype, either as they come through the academy or get poached from rivals, an opportunity off the bench or even a shock start, talk of how they could develop and then a gradual decline of interest.

Chido Obi is the latest to fall into that category. He arrived after his Arsenal contract expired, which was seen as a massive coup. At 15 he was training with the Gunners first-team and the young striker once scored 10 times in a single game as the Arsenal U16s hammered Liverpool 14-3.

He turned down the chance to sign professionally in north London and announced on social media that he was moving to the red side of Manchester. Within five months he became United's third-youngest ever Premier League player, behind only Angel Gomes and Shola Shoretire.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And like those two, he's had to leave Old Trafford for the good of his development. Obi will spend the season on loan at Willem II in Holland after a deal was struck between the two teams. At 18, he still has time on his side, but has already seen a rapid rise and fall in the extremely early part of his career.

A season in the cold

It was under Ruben Amorim that Obi made his debut. The teenage striker had trained with the first team in February of last after scoring a hat-trick in a 5-1 FA Youth Cup win over Chelsea - and less than a week later and Obi was given his full debut, coming on in injury time during United's loss at Tottenham. He was introduced in stoppage time, failing to touch the ball, but it was the first of eight outings.

Seven of those were off the bench with his only start coming in a 4-3 loss against Brentford, he would play the entire game. He was unable to come up with a goal or an assist.

‌



Given the season only had three months left to run the teenager will have seen his number of appearances as a huge positive. It came at a time when United's attacking depth was clearly an issue.

View 4 Images The teenager made his debut at Tottenham in February 2025

Addressing that would prove a positive for the Red Devils, but not for Obi. His eight appearances in 2024/25 didn't serve as a springboard for anything greater and last season he made a grand total of zero outings.

Instead he was bumped back to the U21s. He would play in the high profile FA Youth Cup final between the two Manchester sides four months ago. Obi started alongside JJ Gabriel, who is the latest teenage sensation that is the talk of United.

‌



No player of Obi's age can expect any divine right to play in the first-team, going between that and the youth teams is almost part of the process, but to be so clearly overlooked for an entire campaign won't have filled him with confidence.

And in December 2025, less than a month before Amorim's difficult tenure would end, the Portuguese coach publicly claimed there was an "entitlement" culture among the youth prospects at United.

View 4 Images Ruben Amorim expressed an issue with the culture surrounding Man Utd's youth players

Amorim was keen to point out that Obi had not started every game for the under 21s - which later resulted in Obi posting celebratory pictures of him on social media in response to Amorim’s comments, before later deleting them.

‌



“We as a club sometimes forget who we are," said Amorim. "And that’s the feeling that I have. So I understand everything, it’s the environment, it’s the moment of the players, the kids, they feel entitled. They feel free to respond to the manager with a picture. My office is open. Nobody is coming to talk to me. And that is the way we can solve things."

A change in academy policy?

It is not unfair to suggest that those who played for United have a greater understanding of just how much pride the club have in their academy. The amount of teenagers who made their debut under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was notable - the Norwegian seeing first hand how much impact homegrown players could have during his playing days at Old Trafford.

Under him, 16 academy graduates made their debut, that coming in a period of just under three years. In the four-and-a-half years since his sacking 17 players have made their debut.

View 4 Images Chido Obi would spend last season in the U21 set-up after his first-team exposure, which was short lived

‌



That was with Erik ten Hag and Amorim at the helm, two foreign imports. It was widely reported that parents of players in the academy had concerns over Amorim's willingness to dip into the youth system, and that was only made worse by his "entitled" comments.

That feeling shifted once Michael Carrick came into the building, another former player. Blending the need to win with blooding in your own talent is a tough balance to strike. No one will argue that a Shea Lacey, right this second, is a better player than a Matheus Cunha, a Bryan Mbeumo or an Amad. But they only have the chance to reach that level if they're given minutes.

Obi looks to have fallen foul of the recent wave of attacking talent that has arrived at Old Trafford. Time will tell whether his loan stint away is merely all part of the process, or whether he'll simply be another United youngster who had his moment in the spotlight, and nothing more.

Since 2019 there have been 11 United academy graduates who played two games or less for the club before being moved on. Giving youth a chance is one thing, but keeping it inside your four walls and helping them foster careers is the true mark of a successful pathways system. United need to ensure they don't start giving out goodwill debuts and find ways to harbour the talent they have.

‌

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola and when he could make Liverpool debut
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola and when he could make Liverpool debut

Liverpool are ready to throw Bradley Barcola straight in following his blockbuster transfer with Andoni Iraola eyeing a Friday night debut provided he trains well

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola could make his debut at Portman Road on Monday night

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has backed Bradley Barcola to be available to make his debut on Friday after hailing his desire to move to Anfield.

‌



The Frenchman became the Reds' marquee signing of the summer when he finally moved from PSG in a deal worth £123million following a summer-long transfer chase.

‌



It had looked as if the European champions were going to price out Liverpool such was their hefty valuation, but an agreement was eventually struck and Barcola has become the third £100m-plus-player to move to Merseyside inside the last two summers.

‌



Iraola was keen to bolster his forward line and, despite being absent for PSG amid his uncertain future, the Liverpool boss has stated that a positive training session on Thursday will see him poised to make his first outing for his new team when they head to Ipswich on Friday night.

Manchester City were the biggest spenders, backing new manager Enzo Maresca to the tune of £458m. Most of that was on midfielders, with Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and then Enzo Fernandez all arriving in blockbuster transfers.

Maresca needed a quick start after replacing Pep Guardiola and has that after recording wins over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace.

Sports.title: Chelsea plot move for another ex-Liverpool star despite transfer window closing
Sports.content:
Chelsea plot move for another ex-Liverpool star despite transfer window closing

Chelsea saw Enzo Fernandez leave on deadline day without landing a replacement and Xabi Alonso is now eyeing the free agent market to fill the void

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has left Chelsea to join Man City (Image: Manchester City FC)

Chelsea are weighing up a shock move for Georginio Wijnaldum after seeing Enzo Fernandez leave on deadline day and their move for a replacement fall through.

‌



The Blues were heavily involved in the major headlines on the last day of the transfer window, seeing Fernandez leave for Manchester City in a record £125million deal whilst their pursuit of Lamine Camara at Monaco failed to materialise.

‌



It has left Xabi Alonso light in midfield and, with the window closed, the west Londoners have turned to the free agent market. That has led them to Liverpool's former midfielder Wijnaldum, who left the club in 2021.

‌



Foot Mercato reports that Chelsea have contacted Wijnaldum, now 35, as they prepared to offer him a route back into the Premier League, where he previously played for the Reds and Newcastle.

The Dutchman is on the market having left Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer and Alonso sees him as a good option in the interim given the experience he has in England's top flight - winning the title back in 2020 at Anfield.

‌



Wijnaldum made 277 appearances across his time in England, coming up with crucial goals and proving to be part of a hugely effective Liverpool midfield. He showed he can be still effective and scored 17 times in 34 outings for Al-Ettifaq last season, but didn't earn himself a new deal.

Sports.title: Kyrgios accepts one-month suspension after positive cocaine test
Sports.content:
Nick Kyrgios has accepted ‌and served a reduced, one-month suspension under anti-doping rules after testing positive ‌for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in ​Mallorca.

Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules.

The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon is joined by Annabel Croft and Ryan Harrison to react to the news that Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine and been suspended from the sport

The drug is banned in competition and the former Wimbledon finalist has been provisionally suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play or attend tournaments.

During an ​interview with ITIA investigators, the 31-year-old ⁠explained that his use ⁠of cocaine had "occurred socially" during a night out before he was due ‌to play in Mallorca, the statement said.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a ‌World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory, who stated that the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.

"As a result, the ITIA accepted ⁠that Kyrgios' use of cocaine was ​outside of competition," it added.

The ITIA ​said Kyrgios' suspension ends on Thursday, ​subject to completion of the programme.

Prize money and ⁠ranking points from the Mallorca event will be forfeited.

Cocaine is prohibited in-competition and carries a ⁠provisional suspension.

Kyrgios apologised last month ​on social media for the failed drug ​test, saying he had made a "huge mistake" and took full responsibility for ‌it.

"I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it," Kyrgios said in a post on Instagram.

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

His first-round loss to fellow Australian Adam Walton in Majorca was his last competitive singles outing and one of only four singles matches he has played this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 'Battle of the Sexes' match between Aryna Sabalenka and Kyrgios

'Tormented soul' Kyrgios in firing line

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft described Kyrgios as a "tormented soul" who could now find himself on the receiving end of the very criticism he dished out when Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek were involved in high-profile doping cases.

"He has always struck me as a tormented soul out there, and he is never far from creating headlines," Croft said. "He seems to do that effortlessly.

"There is a lot of criticism being thrown at him right now because he was the one firing arrows at other players who had been banned for a certain amount of time. It is now being directed right back at him."

'Kyrgios needs to find balance'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of Kyrgios' best points of his ATP career

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison believes Kyrgios must strike the right balance between his responsibilities on the court and his downtime off it.

"It is disappointing," Harrison added. "Kyrgios has been such an electric player for so long.

"He is one of those guys. You talk about the 'Big Four', and he was the next in line that the casual fan and observer would talk about because of the way he played, his talent, fearlessness and energy.

"The persona would come out sometimes in the way he handled pressure. Sometimes it wasn't always positive.

"When you are an athlete and training on a regular basis, your life is very structured and regimented.

"When you stop playing and you are not doing that on a week-to-week basis, some players can find it difficult to strike a balance and know, 'When can I go out?'

"I think Nick needs to find that balance and, while it is disappointing, hopefully for his sake, as he takes time away, he can find happiness off the court and be the best he can be."

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz has taken a swipe at the hectic tennis calendar and said he will skip tournaments from now on.

The Spaniard, who returned to action after ​a lengthy layoff due to a wrist injury sustained in April to defend his US Open title, said the demands of the schedule made ​it impossible for players to compete in every major ‌event without risking burnout.

The Spaniard pointed to the absences of other top stars as evidence that the schedule is too demanding and will keep causing injuries.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Carlos Alcaraz against Jaime Faria from the US Open

World No 1 Jannik Sinner and British star Jack Draper are notable absentees at Flushing Meadows along with Holger Rune, Joao Fonseca and a host of other players.

"I took more (time off) than I wanted, to be honest, but you know, seeing how tight the calendar is, obviously I don't want to have this break because (of) an injury," said Alcaraz after coming from a set down to beat Jaime Faria in the second round.

"But in the future, I'm going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all.

"I think they (are) adding more important tournaments. You know, in a way they (are) making us play. You can say 'no'. You can keep one or two.

"You can decide your calendar, but there are some Masters 1000s, some grand slams, and we've been out playing 40 weeks if we got to play every mandatory tournament that the ATP, you know, required us to play.

"So it's impossible, and we are seeing a lot of players getting injured, a lot of players getting tired. If they don't do anything about it, we are going to see even more in the future.

"But for me, taking this break because (of) an injury, it wasn't that good, but you know, what I'm going to say is I'm going to take some breaks and miss some tournaments in the future, for sure."

Sports.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts.

Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts

UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.

UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters.

FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership."

UEFA is trying to oust Mr Infantino from power with a resignation or in the FIFA presidential election in March.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol gives the latest on Gianni Infantino and whether he can continue as the president of FIFA

FIFA's lawyers say: "UEFA's application suffers from a fundamental defect: UEFA seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that UEFA admittedly lacks the authority to initiate."

There is a defence of the attempt to launch the $20bn World Cup subsidiary, which Mr Infantino's senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, called a "bad deal" for football when quitting the role in a statement to Sky News.

Sky News previously revealed there were already plans in June to start to receive up to $4.2bn from private investors in October.

But FIFA's legal filing claims it was "only a proposal" that had to be approved by member associations and the ruling council.

FIFA claims UEFA was acting out of self-interest to protect its own competitions and that any disputes should be handled within football not the courts.

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, UEFA issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership," the document filed in the Southern District of New York court states.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News put questions to FIFA's president in the Dominican Republic after his World Cup sell-off plan was abandoned following a backlash from a number of confederations, including UEFA

"UEFA's economic motivation was to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite.

"If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces UEFA's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments.

"By raising funds to allow some of FIFA's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FIFA Forward Enterprice (FFE) would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad."

Sky Sports News has been told the feeling at UEFA is that if there is nothing to worry about, then why not disclose the documents. It is understood the process could be shortened by disclosing documents relating to FFE plans.

Sports.title: A squad once worth over £1bn! The free agents your club could still sign
Sports.content:
The summer transfer window might be shut, but a host of free agents once worth a combined value of £1.15bn are still available to sign.

Jadon Sancho, Paul Pogba and Dele Alli are among some of the big names on the free agency market, so could your club give them the opportunity to rediscover their once world-class level?

Here, Sky Sports presents a free agent squad packed with World Cup winners, Champions League veterans and domestic league champions…

Values below reflect players' historic peak market value according to transfermarkt.

Starting XI

Goalkeeper: Neto, 38 - £15.5m in 2018

After his year-long loan with Arsenal from Bournemouth ended in 2025, Neto joined Botafogo but decided to terminate his contract by mutual consent in June. His disappointing stint in Brazil was summed up in his final game for the club, receiving a red card for time-wasting and swearing at the referee.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal, 34 - £51.5m in 2018

Arguably one of the best right-backs of his generation, Carvajal left Real Madrid after 23 years this summer. During his time at the Spanish giants, he made 450 appearances, and leaves as one of the most decorated players in history with 27 titles, including six Champions League titles.

Centre-back: Sergio Ramos, 40 - £43m in 2018

Another Real Madrid icon finds himself on the free agent list. Ramos joined Los Blancos in 2005 and spent 16 years at the club, scoring 101 goals in 671 appearances, winning 23 trophies along the way. He's since played for PSG, Sevilla and most recently Mexican side Monterrey, and despite not having had a club since January 2026, the Spanish icon is yet to announce his retirement from football.

Image: World Cup winner Sergio Ramos is a Real Madrid legend

Centre-back: David Alaba, 34 - £55.8m in 2018

Former Bayern Munich and Real Madrid defender Alaba is on the free agent market after Real decided not to renew the 34-year-old's contract this summer. An illustrious career consisting of 35 trophies, including 12 league titles and four Champions Leagues, the Austrian could be an asset to any club looking to bolster their defensive unit.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko, 29 - £36m in 2023

Four-time Premier League winner Zinchenko is without a club since his injury-ridden spell at Ajax reduced the Ukrainian to just 20 minutes on the pitch. He was previously on loan at Nottingham Forest from Arsenal for the 2025/26 season, but Forest decided to cut it short in January after limited game time.

Central midfielder: Paul Pogba, 33 - £85.9m in 2019

The 2018 World Cup-winning midfielder signed for Ligue 1 side Monaco on a two-year deal last summer after serving an 18-month football suspension for a doping offence. However, the contract was terminated this summer by mutual consent.

Image: Paul Pogba is a free agent after leaving Monaco

Central midfielder: Dele Alli, 30 - £85.9m in 2018

The once wonderkid - who produced an 18-goal 2016/17 Premier League campaign for Spurs and helped England reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals - has struggled in recent years with injuries and form. Alli has been without a club since his contract was terminated at Como in 2025 by mutual consent but has yet to officially retire.

Central midfielder: Philippe Coutinho, 34 - £128.8m in 2018

Former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder Coutinho has been a free agent since he left his boyhood club Vasco da Gama in February. The Brazilian struggled to reach the levels he showed at Liverpool since signing for Barcelona in a mega-money move in 2018.

Right-wing: Raheem Sterling, 31 - £137.4m in 2019

Having been released by Feyenoord after just three months, Sterling has been through a difficult period on-and-off the pitch. Last month he was charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide and is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court for a hearing on September 15. Football-wise, he hasn't scored since September 2024, when he bagged Arsenal's fourth in a 5-1 victory over Bolton in the Carabao Cup.

Image: Raheem Sterling joined Feyenoord in February after terminating his Chelsea contract

Left-wing: Jadon Sancho, 26 - £111.6m in 2020

It's been five years since Sancho's £73m move to Man Utd from Borussia Dortmund, and according to Sky in Germany, talks have taken place with his former club after indicating a willingness to join. The winger most recently featured in Aston Villa's Europa League-winning squad.

Striker: Karim Benzema, 38 - £51.5m in 2016

The 2022 Ballon d'Or winner has spent the last three years in Saudi Arabia, spending two-and-a-half years with Al Ittihad before moving to Al Hilal on a one-and-a-half-year deal, which was terminated by mutual agreement this summer.

Substitutes

Riyad Mahrez (£51.5m), Georginio Wijnaldum (£43m), Wilfried Zaha (£47.2m), James Rodriguez (£68.7m), Yves Bissouma (£30m), Tyrell Malacia (£18.9m), Jamie Vardy (£17.2m), Anthony Martial (£55.8m), Chris Smalling (£17.2m).

Keeping hold of Bunny Shaw makes Man City title favourites

Sports.title: England cruise to series win with six-wicket victory in Derby

Sports.title: All right for Wong as England seamer 'keeps things simple'
Sports.content:
England bowler Issy Wong likes delving into her box of tricks - off the field when she completes Rubik's Cubes in next to no time and on it as she tries to get batters out.

But the seamer was rewarded for simplicity on Thursday as a five-wicket haul - her first in international cricket - helped her side wrap up an one-day international series win over Ireland.

Prioritising the wobble-seam delivery that angled in to the right handers, Wong bowled opposition captain Gaby Lewis through the gate for her first strike of the day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wong, as well as Sky Sports pundits Tash Farrant and Ravi Bopara, reflect on the bowler's player-of-the-match display in Derby

Her relentless targeting of the stumps also saw her clean up Leah Paul off an inside edge, while her three other victims, including top-scorer Amy Hunter, were caught.

Wong had struggled for accuracy during England's victory in the series opener at Leicester on Tuesday, conceding four wides in a row as she curled balls too far past off stump.

She was much improved in Derby, and her display enthused Sky Sports Cricket expert Tash Farrant.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of the action from Derby as England raced to a target of 166 in just 23 overs to clinch a series win over Ireland with a game to spare

"She hit the same area every single time and kept things simple," Farrant said of Wong after England's six-wicket victory followed the same result two days earlier.

"Wong was struggling so much with consistency two or so years ago but the reason she got a five-fer here was the consistency. She pretty much hit that bail-trimming length every delivery.

"Sometimes with Wong, I think she has all the skills and wants to show them all. Here, she just bowled those wobble balls angling in towards the stumps."

Could Wong form 'formidable' new-ball pairing with Bell?

With premier seamer Lauren Bell rested for this series, Wong has played her first ODIs since the tour of Ireland in 2024, taking her to six matches in the format in total.

It is about doing what the team needs from me. At the moment, I feel like that is hitting the stumps as much as possible. I am using my wobble seam to help me do that.

She first featured in 50-over cricket for her country back in 2022 but has never been able to grab a regular place, with previous run-up issues contributing to that. Now, though, she has a big opportunity.

Farrant added: "England are looking for someone who can back-up Bell with the new ball and if Wong can be that consistent, they could be a formidable pair going forward."

Farrant's fellow Sky Sports pundit Ravi Bopara does not want Wong to completely jettison the out-swinger, saying having that delivery in her armoury can help her "progress her game to the next level", but her method worked a treat against Ireland.

Image: Wong (right) was playing just her sixth one-day international for England

Wong told reporters: "Even in the last three months, I feel like I've come on a lot. It feels like I've worked quite hard and I guess when you work hard good things happen.

[More responsibility] brings the best out of me. Me and Lauren Filer have got to pick the balls whereas Bell usually does that."

Wong had also spoken when collecting her player-of-the-match award about how chats with staff, including media manager Dean Wilson, had helped her "mindset".

Whoever told her to focus on the wobble seam played a blinder.

Sports.title: Osaka urges US Open influencers to respect tennis 'etiquette'
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka urged the growing number of social media influencers at the US Open to respect the sport's "etiquette" following her second-round win over Katerina Siniakova.

The issue has become a talking point at the tournament following Osaka's opening win over Anastasia Zakharova on Monday, in which viral videos have since surfaced of some influencers not paying attention to the tennis.

After overcoming a mid-match wobble to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1 and reach the third round in New York, Osaka said on the issue: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Naomi Osaka against Katerina Siniakova from the US Open

"I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like [my] first-round match.

"Overall, I think there is huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

Osaka added: "I was going to say, today, the umpire told everyone to be quiet - more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet.

"I do think that in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and stuff, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too."

Osaka wears more understated outfit for second round

Against Siniakova, it wasn't quite as headline-grabbing a display - both on and off the court - from Osaka, who sported a more understated entrance outift, for which she is gaining increasing notoriety.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Osaka had another stylish outfit as she made her entrance ahead of facing Katerina Siniakova in the US Open second round

The two-time US Open champion had turned heads when wearing a long, white skirt and hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her ahead of her tournament opener on Monday night.

But on this occasion, Osaka opted for a more understated, shimmery all-white number which wouldn't have looked out of place at Wimbledon rather than Flushing Meadows.

The 13th seed was swiftly into her stride in the first set, breaking Siniakova to love in the fourth game of the opener, which she clinched with a second break of the Czech.

Osaka appeared to be cruising to victory in the second when breaking for 4-2 and 5-3 leads, only for her serve to desert her at that time as she was broken three times in a row to ultimately drop the set 7-5.

The four-time Gland Slam winner found her footing again for the decider, dropping only one game to clinch her spot in the next round.

Swiatek storms into third round in 71 minutes

Iga Swiatek also stormed into the third round of the US Open, with a clinical 6-3 6-2 win over Nadia Podoroska that took just 71 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Iga Swiatek against Nadia Podoroska from the US Open

It was only the second meeting between the pair - the previous coming in the semi-finals of the 2020 French Open, with Swiatek victorious en route to claiming the first of her six Grand Slam titles.

The 2022 US Open champion, seeded eighth this year in New York, was back to her ruthless best.

She broke in the fourth game of the opening set and pushed on to take it 6-3, before snatching a crucial break of serve in the first game of the second set to ensure that she stayed firmly in control.

Podoroska showed some glimpses of her best form, but Swiatek was rarely under pressure and converted her first match point to book her place in the third round at Flushing Meadows for the seventh-straight time.

Meanwhile, Madison Keys ‌mounted an epic comeback against Anna Bondar, saving five match points before clinching a 5-7 6-4 7-6 (10-5) win to delight ⁠the US home fans.

The 2017 finalist, and 2025 Australian Open winner, sent over a remarkable 34 forehand winners to get the job ‌done and gave all credit to her adoring fans after forcing Bondar into an error at the net on match point.

"That was something, huh?" Keys told the crowd ‌after the win. "No stress though - we all knew I had it, right?"

Auger-Aliassime becomes highest seed to fall

Men's third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime became the highest seed to be knocked out of the US Open so far when suffering a shock second-round exit to unseeded Karen Khachanov.

Khachanov, who reached the semi-final stage in New York in 2022, broke ​Auger-Aliassime's serve seven times on Louis Armstrong Stadium ‌and saved seven of the nine break points he faced en route to securing only his ​second top-10 win at a Grand Slam.

The first set was tight, with neither player giving the other any opportunities, but while Auger-Aliassime - a two-time US Open semi-finalist, including last year - edged it in the tie-break, the Canadian was unable to build on that momentum and won just seven further games.

Khachanov, who lost the opening match ‌in his three tournament tune-up events, produced some of his best tennis to reach the third round in impressive style.

Elsewhere, Taylor Fritz delivered another commanding performance to ‌brush aside Mattia Bellucci 6-0 6-1 6-1, extending his emphatic start to the tournament without dropping ​a set.

Fritz is among a handful of contenders looking to end a 23-year American wait for ​a men's Grand Slam singles champion, and the ninth seed has only strengthened his position ​after his first two matches.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
Can Wirtz find his best for Liverpool?

Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. It is clear the German needs to become more influential as a No 10 given the quality of players he has around him, especially after the expensive arrival of Bradley Barcola this week. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to start. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin

Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

Red Bull gives you wings

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and, more recently, RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is looking for his first back-to-back league wins with Newcastle. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Bees plot left-wing raid on Black Cats

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris

Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

Chema looks another astute Brighton buy

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. Signed for £18.9m, it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH

Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

An early basement battle at the Cottage

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to join them. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH

Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

O’Reilly to step into Rodri role for City?

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

Delap to be thrown in against shaky Spurs

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21 international is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against a fragile opponent could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared to Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU

Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

Six points, seven signings for happy Hull

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU

Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

View image in fullscreen Elliot Stroud, one of Hull’s 19 summer signings, in action during their 1-0 win at Coventry. Photograph: Neal Simpson/Getty Images/Allstar

Everton fans react to dismal deadline day

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights following the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, the Friedkin Group, in the firing line following the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter

Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

Chelsea face litmus test in London derby

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time that Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But having come close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has already conceded five goals can keep out the champions at the other end. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 14: West Ham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 11th (NB: this is not necessarily Suzanne Wrack’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

West Ham were in big trouble last December, with half the season gone and one win in 11 games. Rehanne Skinner was dismissed and the former Italy forward Rita Guarino came in to steady the ship. There were questions over how much any manager would be able to do without the club giving a bit more support to the women’s setup, but Skinner, fairly or not, had lost the dressing room and heads were down. The impact of Guarino wasn’t instant, a 5-0 defeat by Chelsea was a cruel introduction. It took a little time to rebuild the confidence of the team and get them playing the way she believed they could, but back-to-back wins against Newcastle in the FA Cup and Leicester in the Women’s Super League followed the Chelsea game, before a huge 3-2 win against Brighton and battling draws with Manchester United and London City Lionesses contributed to 14 points from their final 11 WSL games, taking their total to 19.

As players started to depart in the summer, the situation looked bleak. Among the 14 departures were the forward Shekiera Martinez, who joined Tottenham, Katrina Gorry, who decided to take a break from football, and Shelina Zadorsky, who left at the end of her contract before signing for AFC Toronto. Then the signings started to arrive and suddenly the dark clouds were parting.

The Hammers have had a hugely productive and impressive window with 10 signings, including the forwards Kelly Gago, recruited from Everton, and Ebony Salmon, who joined from Aston Villa, the defenders Estelle Cascarino, whose loan was made permanent, and Nadine Riesen and Laia Codina, who joined from Eintracht Frankfurt and Arsenal respectively, and the young English talents Sienna Wareing and Niamh Peacock who signed from Manchester United and Arsenal. Guarino has been backed in this window and West Ham have a real opportunity to make a statement in the WSL.

Off-field picture

West Ham’s relative indifference towards their women’s team has been long known. There has been a steady decline since the departure of the enthusiastic Jack Sullivan as managing director of the women’s team in 2021 – the son of David Sullivan having been handed control of the side at 18. Little is known of how cash strapped the women’s setup is compared with other WSL sides. The club have not published detailed financial figures throughout their time in the WSL, with their most recent Companies House submission saying they are entitled to exemption from audit under section 479A of the Companies Act 2006. According to Football Association figures they were the WSL’s lowest spenders on agents’ fees in the year to February 2026, at £97,000, and one of only two clubs – Manchester United were the other – whose spend was down year on year.

The manager

Guarino was a relative unknown when she arrived in the WSL, having managed only in Italy. In the second half of the season West Ham didn’t quite experience a new manager bounce, but Guarino was able to guide them to another four wins and a 10th-place finish above Liverpool and Leicester. Guarino has impressed. Codina told the BBC of her transfer talks: “I remember having my first conversation with Rita. It was at the beginning of everything. I had my agent next to me and I was like: ‘Wow.’ The feeling that I got in this meeting is what I want in my future; it is what I want for my next steps.”

Star signing

Gago scored 10 goals in 30 games for Everton but was frustrated there, handing in a written transfer request in January. The 27-year-old has praised West Ham, saying: “The family feel of the club really appealed to me and I’m excited to join that family. I’m going to give everything in order to help the team reach our ambitions and I’m really looking forward to getting started.”

Stat attack

West Ham were the most direct team last season. They moved the ball upfield quicker than anyone and only Leicester averaged fewer passes per possession sequence. There is no right way to play; everyone needs a style. But after West Ham collected fewer points than in three of the preceding four campaigns, is it time for a change of approach?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

Inès Belloumou played 18 times for West Ham last season after a long wait following her recruitment from Bayern Munich in July 2024. She was sent out on loan straight away, first to Lazio then to Malmö to build up the points to meet the governing body endorsement criteria for international player visas. This summer the 25-year-old, who was born in France and represented the country up to under-23 level before switching allegiance to Algeria, shone at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. Named in the team of the tournament, Belloumou started all six Algeria games as they finished third, with the full-back scoring the winning penalty in the shootout at the end of the third-place playoff. Full of confidence, she is ready to kick on in the WSL.

View image in fullscreen Full-back Inès Belloumou crunches into a challenge with Arsenal’s Smilla Holmberg. Photograph: Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images

What they say

“I want to put the club in the highest position in the table and go as far as we can in the cups. For me, the WSL is the best league in the world at the moment and anything can happen. Anything is possible. We need to have a lot of consistency, which is not easy, but it’s why we work hard every day” – Viviane Asseyi, after signing a new contract

Where are they playing their home games?

If you spend too much time dwelling on this you’ll feel as if you’re in Waiting for Godot. The team have not played at the club’s main stadium since a 2-0 loss to Tottenham in front of close to 25,000 fans in September 2019. There has been talk since of it being a priority, including from Skinner, but every year another season ticks on without the team playing at the club’s main home. Instead, the team continue to call Dagenham and Redbridge’s Victoria Road stadium home.

Sports.title: Mike Dean claims he played secret games for a laugh while refereeing matches
Sports.content:
The former Premier League referee Mike Dean claims he used to take part in secret challenges while officiating, including trying to stay in the centre circle for as long as possible, as he confessed to “just joking about” during matches. The remarks, made by one of the most well-known officials in the English game, have been met with bemusement by refereeing officials who say there is no evidence of any such behaviour having ever taken place.

Dean was a member of the select group of referees for more than two decades before he retired in 2022 and a brief spell as a video assistant referee followed. In an interview on Jamie Vardy’s podcast this week, Dean shared anecdotes from his time as a top-flight official in the pre-VAR era. “We used to say, ‘We’ll kick off now. Right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle,’” he said. “I’ve done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously – [I] went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle.

“I used to do another thing. I used to stand in the centre circle – see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about. I got about 15 minutes once.”

Officials within the refereeing organisation, Pro Ref, are understood to be puzzled by the claims, with the suggestion that a referee could stay in the centre circle for 15 minutes without someone noticing, for example, seen as highly improbable.

This is not the first time that Dean has courted controversy in a post-retirement interview. Dean was stood down from his role as a VAR in 2023 after failing to intervene over an error in a match between Tottenham and Chelsea, refereed by Anthony Taylor. Describing Taylor as a “mate”, Dean told Simon Jordan’s podcast that he had chosen not to ask Taylor to review his decision on a VAR monitor because he didn’t want him to have “any more grief than he already had”.

Dean earned notoriety during his time as a referee for his flamboyant mannerisms and apparent eye for the camera – as captured in the terrace chant “Mike Dean, it’s all about you”. But he was also held to be one of the best officials in the top flight, taking charge of 561 matches – and issuing a record 114 red cards – over the course of his 22-year career.

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli leaves Arsenal for Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in £60m deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal have confirmed Gabriel Martinelli has joined the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for £60m. It is understood the deal for Brazil forward includes a sell-on clause.

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Ituano in 2019, has fallen down the pecking order at the Emirates despite being part of the squad that won the Premier League title last season. His fee surpasses the previous record £40m received by Arsenal when they sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017.

Quick Guide How do I 

Martinelli is believed to have signed a four-year contract worth about £17m a season. His move was widely expected after Arsenal agreed a deal last week and has gone through before the transfer window in Saudi Arabia closes on Sunday.

The 25-year-old joins his Brazil teammate Gabriel Jesus in leaving Arsenal this week, the striker having moved to Barcelona for £8.6m. The Premier League champions also sold Fábio Vieira to Hamburg on deadline day but decided against bringing in players.

Arsenal are believed to have received about £3m from Brook Norton-Cuffy’s £14m move from Genoa to Hull owing to a sell-on clause in the England Under-21 defender’s contract but missed out on about £7m when Folarin Balogun move to Everton collapsed.

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker not a part of their plans for the season. They could have accommodated him for the first-half of the campaign because one of their 17 senior non-homegrown players – Xavi Simons – is out until March or April, according to the manager, Roberto Di Zerbi, with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Spurs made clear to Richarlison before the closure of the transfer window in England on Tuesday night that he would not be included so he could arrange a move. He was unable to do so, with one to his former club, Everton, not happening. He is the subject of firm interest from Trabzonspor in Turkey, where the window remains open until Friday night.

Richarlison posted a message on social media on Monday in which he said he would not allow anybody to decide his future for him. He talked about his commitment to Spurs; how “when everything here was falling apart and they needed me, I stayed and gave my life”.
