Richarlison was Spurs’ top scorer in the league last season with 11 goals. He also said: “So I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I’ve always had for the Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola defends Liverpool opting against throwing ‘crazy money’ at short-term fixes
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has defended Liverpool’s summer transfer strategy and said the club were right not to pay “crazy money” for short-term fixes while Hugo Ekitiké, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are recovering from serious injuries.

Liverpool had the highest net spend in the Premier League, with Bradley Barcola, signed for a potential £123m, added on Monday to a front line that includes the £125m Alexander Isak and £116m Florian Wirtz. Barcola could make his debut at Ipswich on Friday, despite not featuring for Paris Saint-Germain this season.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Liverpool’s outlay did not include a right-back, defensive midfielder or right-winger but Iraola, who believes Barcola could be deployed in Mohamed Salah’s old position on the right, insisted he had no qualms with the squad at his disposal.

“I’m very happy with all the signings we’ve made,” said the Liverpool head coach. “I know the next question: ‘Do you want more signings in other positions?’ At the end the club has decided those signings we have done are the ones that improved our team and our position.

“There were other options we decided not to take, for different reasons: sometimes it is sporting reasons because they don’t improve what you have, sometimes it is economical reasons as it didn’t make sense in terms of the market to do those movements. But I’m happy now I know what we have, I have a lot of quality in the team and now it is the moment for us, for the players, for me to develop what we have.”

Leoni has been sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament injury since last September but is expected to resume first-team training during the international break, which starts this month. There is no date on Bradley’s and Ekitiké’s return from serious knee and achilles injuries respectively, but Iraola said the club had to plan for the long term and wait for all three to recover.

Iraola said: “The club has decided not to sign someone because we need them for these two or three months and instead trust the players we have, us working with the players we have and thinking of the long term.

“Yes, as a manager you need the players for today but if they [the club] explain to you the vision and the long-term project, you also have to understand the club. Sometimes it doesn’t make sense to pay crazy money – the market was the market – for players who maybe in the long term you don’t need. Then you will need this money to solve other problems in that position. Sometimes it’s better to look a little bit further than the next game and the next month.”

Despite the absence of a natural right-winger – Liverpool explored deals for Yankuba Minteh at Brighton and Ismaïla Sarr at Crystal Palace – Iraola is confident Barcola, Victor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha will provide sufficient cover.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He said: “I think we’ve preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position. I’m very used from my previous teams to demand for all the wingers to play both sides.

“Probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific from the left side, but I think he has also showed the willingness to improve and play on the right. Even Bradley, he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.”

Sports.title: ‘It’s huge’: Nike deal breaks new ground in WSL for London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League club London City Lionesses’ new front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike is the largest in the women’s game, according to their American owner, Michele Kang.

The length and value of the deal has not been disclosed but sources close to the WSL club are hailing it as a gamechanging moment and Kang claims that it even exceeds some men’s Premier League clubs’ shirt deals.

London City, who host Manchester United on Friday in the opening game of the new WSL campaign, are about to embark on only their second top-flight season, but this summer they have shocked the sport by signing a flurry of some of the biggest names in women’s football, including the former Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas, the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Putellas’ Spain and Barcelona teammate, Mapi León.

It has been reported that the largest current front-of-shirt sponsorship deal for a women’s football team is an approximately $4m per year agreement reached by the new NWSL franchise in Atlanta – who will begin competing in 2028, but Kang told BBC Sport: “I can absolutely confirm that this is the largest women-only front-of-shirt deal. It is higher than the Atlanta number.

“I can absolutely also share that it is higher than some of the men’s Premier League front-of-shirt deals. It’s huge. That’s why it is landmark. There are so many other people who believe in the future of women’s football. They [Nike] didn’t make this decision lightly. They did not write a charity cheque. They believe in the future and they believe together we will invest and build this future together.”

View image in fullscreen Michele Kang has been London City Lionesses owner since December 2023. Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty Images

The deal will be a major boost to London City’s finances. In their most recent set of financial accounts, they posted an annual revenue of just £902,000 for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion to the top flight. Their operating loss was over £10m, and more than 10 times that revenue.

Their transfer business has attracted questions about how they can fit their lavish spending within the salary cap, as the WSL’s rules dictate that clubs cannot spend more on their player wage bills than 80% of their relevant revenue plus up to £4m of owner contributions. But it is understood this Nike deal will transform their annual revenue astronomically compared to previous seasons.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The popularity on social media of their biggest new signing Alexia Putellas – who has 3.4 million Instagram followers – and Earps and León is believed to have been a major driving factor in the supposedly high valuation from Nike. Putellas has helped Spain win 2023’s World Cup and won the Champions League four times with Barcelona. The Spaniard shared the news of the sponsorship on her Instagram account on Thursday.

Sports.title: Thierry Henry says players ‘have more power than they think’ amid Fifa scandals
Sports.content:
As Fifa continues to face scrutiny from some confederations and fans, Thierry Henry has encouraged players to use their voice as the political battle for control of international soccer unfolds. The former Arsenal and Barcelona forward turned pundit spoke with the Guardian on Tuesday alongside Kate Scott and Jamie Carragher as CBS and Paramount prepare for this season’s Champions League broadcasts.

“For me, the players have more power than they think they have,” Henry said when asked for his thoughts on the situation. “And if they want it to change, they can make it happen – especially nowadays.”

Fifa has been under public duress in the wake of multiple scandals surrounding the 2026 World Cup, exacerbated further after reports of Gianni Infantino’s effort to sell the World Cup’s commercial rights. The ensuing month has seen the Fifa president face significant criticism, with Uefa exploring potential legal options against Infantino.

Scott, who anchors the CBS panel comprising Henry, Carragher and Micah Richards, spoke extensively about 2021’s attempted Super League project and the ensuing debacle in an Apple TV documentary. The Super League saga seemed to pit the business interests of the sport’s business class against the game’s heart, represented by players, coaches and fans. The latest situation involving Fifa has progressed in a similar spirit.

“I think it’s going to be really interesting to see [what comes next],” Scott said. “I think probably a large portion of world football has come to a point where they would like to see a change in [the Fifa presidency], similarly to the way we felt about [the Super League] … I think if you’re invested in the game and you love the game, it just kind of leaves a bad taste.”

Infantino has been re-elected twice since 2016, both times without a challenger. The next vote is slated for 18 March 2027, with no alternative having declared their candidacy.

“I have no idea which way that will go, because obviously one thing that Gianni Infantino has proven to be within world football is a very smart power broker and has understood how to make allies, use those allies to his benefit,” Scott said.

For Henry, though, the voice of the players can – and should – be a bigger part of the conversation.

“Players have all the power if they want to, and sometimes they don’t, I think, use it or realize actually the power that they have,” Henry said. “You guys in the US know fully well: when the player wants to do something, the league listens. You saw it with the NBA. You saw it with the NFL … At one point, the players are always on the side: go entertain, take your money, leave.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Us debating about it here, what’s going to change? We can all have a view whether it’s a good one or a bad one … But for me, the players have more power than they think they have. And if they want it to change, they can make it happen – especially nowadays.”

Sports.title: Daniel Kretinsky to become biggest West Ham shareholder in blow to Amanda Staveley
Sports.content:
Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the biggest shareholder at West Ham after striking an agreement with David Sullivan, dealing a blow to Amanda Staveley’s hopes of buying a stake in the Championship club.

Staveley was a guest at the London Stadium for West Ham’s 4-2 win over Wolves earlier this week and was pushing to buy Vanessa Gold’s 25.1% stake in the club. The British businesswoman, previously a director at Newcastle, had struck a deal with the Gold family in July and was fronting a consortium looking for a way on to the east London club’s board.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

However that arrangement sparked a process allowing West Ham’s other shareholders to exercise their pre-emption rights over the Gold family’s stake before a 5.30pm deadline on Thursday evening. It is believed that Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire and the owner of Royal Mail, and Sullivan have come to an agreement that will see the former increase his 27% stake to 46%. Sources have said there is unlikely to be a way back for Staveley’s group.

Sources have consistently said that Kretinsky, who will surpass Sullivan as the biggest shareholder, is determined to increase his interest in West Ham as they look to rebuild after their relegation from the Premier League last season. His plans were complicated by Staveley entering the picture.

However it is understood that Sullivan rebuffed an inquiry from Staveley about buying his stake during the summer. The 77-year-old privately indicated a preference to deal with Kretinsky, who first bought a stake in West Ham in November 2021. The arrangement will see Sullivan increase his stake from 38.8% to 40%, making him the second largest shareholder. The American businessman Tripp Smith’s stake will go from 8% to 11% and the remaining shareholders will rise from 1.1% to 3%. Staveley would need shareholders not to take up their pre-emption rights to have a chance of making a separate offer for the Gold shares.

Sullivan stepped down as a director and co-chair of West Ham in June, before a joint investigation by the Times and Panorama reporting on seven women abusing his power and preying on them for sex in claims that date back to the 1980s and 90s. The 77-year-old categorically denies the allegations. Sullivan has been present at West Ham’s home games this season but does not have a seat on the board and is no longer the most powerful person at the club.

Sports.title: Taylor Harwood-Bellis left out of Champions League squad just days after joining Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Taylor Harwood-Bellis left out of Champions League squad just days after joining Aston Villa

Aston Villa have named their squad for the Champions League league phase, but Taylor Harwood-Bellis was not included.

The decision has come only days after the centre-back completed his summer move from Southampton.

2 Harwood-Bellis has missed out on Villa's league phase squad Credit: Getty

Harwood-Bellis put pen to paper in a deal worth an initial £25million, with another £5m in add-ons also included.

However, he will not play in the opening stage of their Champions League campaign.

Also omitted from the squad was centre-back Modou Keba Cisse and teenage striker Brian Madjo, who scored for Villa against Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup.

As listed on the UEFA website, 23 players have been selected for Villa's league phase matches.

Their squad includes nine of their signings from the summer window, which closed on Tuesday night.

Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Leon Goretzka, Joao Gomes, Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Alejandro Garnacho and Ibrahim Mbaye are all available for selection.

Could Harwood-Bellis still play in the Champions League?

Although he cannot feature during the league phase, Harwood-Bellis could still play later on in the competition.

Clubs who qualify for the knockout stages can register a maximum of three new players in their primary List A.

However, the squad must still have a maximum of 25 players in total.

Harwood-Bellis could even find himself involved in Villa's plans during the league phase.

2 Emery has selected his squad for this season's competition Credit: Getty

An outfield player named on List A can be replaced should they suffer a long-term injury or illness that lasts at least 60 days.

Clubs can temporarily replace just one outfield player and bring in a new one from the first match up to and including the sixth.

This means that, if one of Villa's selected centre-backs was ruled out for 60 or more days, then Harwood-Bellis could replace them.

Who will Villa play in the Champions League?

The league phase draw was conducted on August 27, with Unai Emery and his side learning their eight opponents.

Villa first travel to Club Brugge before back-to-back home matches against Fenerbahce and Viking FK.

Tough tests at Galatasaray and Barcelona follow, and then reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain are their final test of 2026.

Borussia Dortmund and Slavia Prague cap off their league phase, where a top-eight finish would send them into the knockouts.

Sports.title: Will Enzo Fernandez start for Man City immediately after £125m Chelsea transfer?
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez is the joint most expensive player in British football history after his mega-money move from Chelsea to Manchester City.

And the £125m midfielder will be itching to make his debut for his new club.

2 Fernandez has been reunited with his old Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca at Man City Credit: AFP

Man City, who have won their first two Premier League games under Enzo Maresca, are back in action at home to Coventry on Saturday.

Will Fernandez start for Man City against Coventry?

Following the summer arrivals of Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi – also for substantial fees – City certainly have no shortage of quality options in midfield.

Anderson started the wins over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace, with Bouaddi replacing him from the bench for his debut late on in the latter game.

And while 18-year-old Bouaddi is undoubtedly one of the most prodigious midfield talents around, Maresca may feel a need to ease him into the rigours of the Premier League.

Fernandez, by contrast, has been there and done it, spending the last three-and-a-half years with Chelsea.

He's also got some minutes in the tank already this term, making what proved to be his final appearance for the Blues as a substitute in their opening-weekend win at Fulham.

As such, one would expect him to be in contention to start for City this weekend.

That could be bad news for Nico O'Reilly, who started in a more advanced midfield role against Bournemouth before playing deeper against Palace.

And with Josko Gvardiol starting the campaign so well in the England international's slightly more natural left-back role, scoring the winner against Bournemouth and providing an assist last time out, O'Reilly may have to make do with a spot on the bench for the visit of Coventry.

Will City's other new signings play?

City have made two other signings since their last outing, both wingers.

2 City won the race to sign Ndiaye Credit: Getty

Brazilian Allan joined from Palmeiras on the penultimate day of the transfer window, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving from Everton on deadline day.

But neither is likely to dislodge Phil Foden or Antoine Semenyo – both of whom set up goals in the 4-1 victory over Palace – so will probably find themselves among the substitutes in the first instance.

What has Enzo Fernandez said?

Speaking after completing his switch to City, Fernandez expressed his desire to go to another level. He said: "I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

"If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

"I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here."

What have City fans said?

The signing of Fernandez has divided opinion among City fans following his antics for Argentina at the World Cup.

But one supporter who's certainly excited to have him onboard is Noel Gallagher, who told talkSPORT he admired Fernandez's 'ballsy' nature.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer

Troy Deeney believes Viktor Gyokeres considers himself fortunate to remain an Arsenal player now the transfer window has closed.

The striker was linked with a summer exit just a year after becoming a Gunner with his £63.7million move from Sporting.

2 Gyokeres has not played a single minute in the league this season Credit: Getty

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez became a dream target for the Premier League champions amid fellow interest from Barcelona.

talkSPORT reported that, to supplement a potential deal, Arsenal explored the possibility of offering Gyokeres during their initial talks.

Alvarez did not sign for the Gunners and, therefore, Gyokeres did not leave, with Mikel Arteta insisting that he would remain at the club.

However, the Sweden international has not featured in either of their Premier League victories against Coventry City and Aston Villa.

Kai Havertz has been the preferred option up top so, with Gyokeres struggling for minutes, Deeney senses he has had some fortune.

"I think he knows he's lucky to be there, personally," he said on the Premier League All Access podcast for talkSPORT.

"I think when you look at his career, look at his attributes, he's probably going, 'I'm at a team here, I've won the Premier League, this is unbelievable'.

"He will be used in the Champions League, but also there's a business element to this where sometimes, things just get swept under the rug now.

"He'll have a conversation, I wouldn't be surprised if we start seeing over the next two, three weeks, he gets more minutes and more time now the window's closed.

"Mikel is not stupid enough to just keep him on the outside, he'll be like, 'Alright, you're still here, you're part of the squad, let's move forward.'"

2 Havertz sits top of the pecking order at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Could Gyokeres play for Arsenal against Chelsea?

After being an unused substitute in the wins over Coventry and Villa, Gyokeres is waiting for his first league appearance.

Havertz was quiet at Villa Park as he managed just one shot, but he is likely to return to the starting XI this weekend.

Arsenal host Chelsea in the headline Premier League clash on Sunday, with both sides having a 100 per cent record thus far.

Gyokeres looks set to be named on the bench for a third consecutive match, but could earn his first outing.

Now that Gabriel Jesus has left for Barcelona, the 28-year-old joins Havertz as the only striker options at Arsenal.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho handed Jesse Lingard warning amid ‘fascinating’ free transfer links
Sports.content:
Jadon's Sancho's rumoured move to Brazilian club Palmeiras would be 'fascinating' were it to come to fruition.

That's the view of South American football expert Tim Vickery, with Sancho linked with a surprise switch to the three-time Copa Libertadores winners.



2 Sancho's last appearance for Manchester United came in the 2024 Community Shield Credit: Getty

The winger is a free agent after leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract this summer.

And should he head to Brazil, he'll follow in the footsteps of former United teammate Jesse Lingard, who joined Corinthians back in March.

Vickery keen on Sancho to Palmeiras

However, Vickery stressed that it wouldn't be the same kind of move – with Lingard now 33 and Sancho, at 26, still theoretically in his prime.



He told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs: "They've [Palmeiras] got a week to sort this one out [the Brazilian transfer window closes next Friday, September 11].

"Jesse Lingard is over here with Corinthians. He's not done very much; he's not getting a game. But obviously Jadon Sancho is at a very different stage in his career.



"They've just sold Allan to Man City, picked up one or two injuries…it would be fascinating, it really would. I'm hoping it happens.

"They're in three competitions. Top of the Brazilian league, quarter-finals of the Libertadores, semi-finals of the Brazilian Cup.



"There's loads and loads to play for, so he can keep himself in the international shop window coming over on a short-term deal.

"Bring it on – I'd love to see it happen."

Sancho's United nightmare

Sancho joined Man United from Borussia Dortmund for £73m in 2021 but failed to live up to his price tag.

2 Sancho signed for Man United when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was manager Credit: Getty

After two unconvincing seasons with Old Trafford, during which he dropped out of the England squad, he was loaned back to Dortmund in 2023.



Further loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa followed, but Sancho looked a shadow of the player he was during his breakthrough years in the Bundesliga.

A move to Brazil would be a left-field one, but it could be just what he needs to kickstart his career – away from the glaring limelight of the European game.

Trailblazing Lingard

Lingard became the first Englishman to play in the Brazilian top flight when he arrived after leaving South Korea's FC Seoul at the end of last year.

He is, however, one of a number of European players currently plying their trade in the Brasileirao.



They include another of Lingard's former United colleagues, Netherlands striker Memphis Depay, who has been at Corinthians since 2024, and ex-Chelsea and Spain midfielder Saul of Flamengo.

Sports.title: Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order
Sports.content:
Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order

Estevao Willian could be growing impatient at Chelsea following the signing of fellow attacker Morgan Rogers.

That's according to Tim Vickery, with the Brazilian starlet facing new competition in his second season at Stamford Bridge.

3 It's not been an easy start for Estevao at Chelsea this season Credit: Getty

After officially arriving from Palmeiras last summer, Estevao delivered a hugely impressive debut campaign in English football at Chelsea.

He played 36 times, scored eight goals and assisted four others as he turned into one of the most exciting Premier League prospects.

A hamstring injury ended his season early and he missed out on the World Cup with Brazil having looked set to be named in their squad.

Over the summer, Chelsea made the club-record £117million signing of Rogers, who is best friends with his England co-star Cole Palmer.

The duo started in their league wins over Fulham and Brighton, as well as the Carabao Cup victory against Luton Town.

Estevao on the other hand has earned just one start and, although it is still early in the season, the 19-year-old may just be slightly restless.

Has Estevao become 'impatient' at Chelsea?

Speaking to talkSPORT, South American football journalist Vickery addressed the potential unhappiness and said: "He chose Chelsea.

"It's the first real, genuine, Brazilian superstar to choose Chelsea over the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

"Maybe he just feels that he's fallen a little bit down the pecking order with Morgan Rogers, who is Cole Palmer's great mate, coming in.

"So, maybe there's a little bit of impatience there, we will find out.

3 Palmer and Rogers have become a go-to attacking pair at Chelsea Credit: Getty

"It is a shame because he gave us some fantastic (performances)... the injury is unfortunate, because I wonder what he might have done at the World Cup because (Carlo) Ancelotti loves him.

"Running into that injury was a little bit unfortunate, but it's doubly unfortunate for me if Chelsea can't give him a regular gig because I think he's just a fantastic talent."

Rogers and Palmer success this season

With both players academy graduates at Manchester City, Rogers and Palmer reunited at club level when the former signed for Chelsea.

They made an excellent start to the season in the 3-2 win at Fulham as each player found the target, whilst Palmer also bagged an assist.

Rogers provided for Pedro Neto in the 4-3 triumph against Brighton, whilst his long-term friend scored a second.

It was a quiet night at the office for the pair when they hosted Luton.

3 Estevao will hope for more regular minutes as the season progresses Credit: Getty

Instead, it was Estevao who impressed for Xabi Alonso's side as his shot went off Hakeem Odoffin for an own-goal during the 2-0 win.

Alonso is likely to stick with Rogers and Palmer playing alongside the in-form Joao Pedro when they visit Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: Chelsea announce signing of Brazilian prodigy 48 hours after transfer window shuts
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of 18-year-old Brazilian full-back Denner from Corinthians.

Denner, who starred for Corinthians' Under-20 side, has signed an eight-year deal with the Blues.

2 Denner will link up with Chelsea's age-group squads at their Cobham training base Credit: Getty

The teenager will link up with Cobham Next Gen (CNG), Chelsea's newly rebranded Under-19 and Under-21 squads.

Denner's rapid rise

Denner joined the youth set-up of hometown club Corinthians at the age of 13.

By 16, he was representing them at U-20 level, helping that team finish as runners-up in the Sao Paulo Youth Cup.

He scored the opening goal in the final as Corinthians were beaten by Sao Paulo.

Chelsea reportedly first agreed a deal for Denner back in 2025 with a view to signing him this year.

He's one of three academy signings the Blues have made this summer, following midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan and defender Alfie Osborne from Hearts.

An attack-minded full-back whose naturally position is on the left, Denner has played for Brazil up to Under-17 level.

He was part of the squad that won the 2025 South American Under-17 Championship.

According to Brazilian media, Denner is a cousin of Arsenal star Gabriel.

And if he follows anything like the career trajectory of the Premier League title-winning Gunners centre-back, Chelsea have a very special talent indeed on their hands.

2 Gabriel may come up against a family member in the next few years Credit: Getty

Chelsea's lucrative window

This summer's transfer window was another hugely busy one for Chelsea.

As well as spending over £300m to bring in players such as Moran Rogers and Maxence Lacroix, the Blues made around £400m in player sales.

A substantial chunk of their total income came from the sale of Enzo Fernandez alone.

The midfielder joined Manchester City on deadline day for £125m.

That fee equalled the record in British football paid by Liverpool to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle last year.

Tosin Adarabioyo and Marc Guiu also made deadline-day moves away from Stamford Bridge, heading to Tottenham and RB Leipzig respectively.

Sports.title: ‘Toothless’ Premier League side warned of relegation threat after ‘uninspiring’ transfer window
Sports.content:
Fulham are heading towards Premier League relegation and showed a lack of motivation in the summer transfer window.

That's the view of talkSPORT host Max Scott as the west London side bemoan a worrying start to the season with two defeats in two.



4 Fulham could be battling for Premier League survival this season Credit: Getty

After a 3-2 home loss to local rivals Chelsea, Sunderland beat Fulham 1-0 on Sunday to ensure they remain without a point in the league.

With Liverpool and Manchester United two of their upcoming tests, new boss Alvaro Arbeloa faces an uphill climb at Craven Cottage.

But, even with 36 more games to play this season, Scott can only see one outcome for the Cottagers - relegation to the Championship.



Speaking on NO BS for talkSPORT, he explained why he tipped Fulham to finish in the bottom three of the Premier League amid their poor start.

"We're going to talk about Sunderland v Fulham," Scott said.

"For me, it was a relegation six-pointer. I have backed Hull, Sunderland and Fulham to go down.



"I'm questioning Hull, I'm not so sure about Sunderland, I still think they're going to be down there. Fulham? They're absolute goners."

Co-host Olly Clink labelled the Cottagers 'terrible' as Scott continued: "Limp-wristed, and no wonder Arbeloa has already lost his rag in his post-match comments after the game.



"I just think... I know this sounds harsh, but what are Fulham?"

Do Fulham regret losing Marco Silva?

Scott once again tipped Fulham for the drop, and then questioned why the club didn't do enough to keep former manager Silva.

4 Arbeloa is winless in the Premier League Credit: Getty

4 Fulham may be left to rue letting Silva leave Credit: Getty

The Portuguese left at the end of last season amid the expiration of his contract in June and is now at Benfica, where has won six of his nine games in charge.



Arbeloa replaced him following a spell at Real Madrid, but it's his predecessor who Scott believes that Fulham should have backed.

Max Scott labels Fulham a 'waste of space'

"Just toothless," Scott said.

"I think, what are they doing not throwing the money at Marco Silva? They have a lot of money in the bank, their owner (Shahid Khan) does. Their stadium, the amount of money they charge Fulham fans...

"They're a waste of space. Give it to Birmingham, give it to Wrexham, that spot, give it to a big club like Sheffield Wednesday in a couple of years if they can get there.

"I just think Fulham are a bit boring. I would never tune into a Fulham game, because Fulham are playing. I would tune into watch Forest play them... I'm just a bit bored of them.



Fulham signings in summer 2026 Gonzalo Garcia - £34m, Real Madrid Shea Charles - £30m, Southampton David Affengruber - £8.6m, Elche Cesar Palacios - £8m, Real Madrid Jonah Kusi-Asare - £5m, Bayern Munich Manuel Angel - £3m, Real Madrid Hugo Larsson - Loan, Eintracht Frankfurt

4 Arbeloa has Fulham sitting 16th in the table Credit: Getty

"And their window has been so uninspiring as well."

"It's a lovely ground," he added. "I've heard from a few players that they really like playing at Fulham, because you don't get the pressure.

"But sometimes, pressure creates diamonds, and there's no diamonds at Fulham at the minute.

"I think they miss the edge that Marco Silva brings, I think they failed to support him adequately in the window, and no wonder he's gone to Benfica.



"If he had been supported, they should have been playing European football and that would have then elevated the club in terms of revenue, players, being an attractive proposition.

"Now, I think they're just going to pale into insignificance in the Premier League and get relegated."

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder

Daniel Kretinsky has agreed a deal with the Gold family to become West Ham's majority shareholder, talkSPORT understands.

As such, Amanda Staveley, who helped lead the Saudi-backed 2024 takeover of Newcastle, has effectively been blocked from buying a stake in the Hammers.



2 Kretinsky is now the Hammers' majority shareholder Credit: Getty

talkSPORT also understands David Sullivan has increased his ownership of the club to 40 per cent.

Following the death of co-chairman David Gold in 2023, his daughter Vanessa took control of a 25.1 per cent share in the club.

Kretinsky's fresh investment

Czech businessman Kretinsky first invested in West Ham back in 2021.

His stake is now set to increase beyond Sullivan's 40 per cent share.

talkSPORT reported last month that Kretinsky had reduced his stake from 27 per cent to below 25 per cent in an effort to prevent Staveley from investing.



The billionaire is believed to have sold part of his share to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

A consortium led by Staveley had been eyeing up the Gold family's stake, worth around £150m.



Sullivan was forced to step down as West Ham chairman in June after accusations of sexual abuse were made against him.

The 77-year-old, who made much of his fortune in the adult entertainment industry, has vehemently denied the claims.



West Ham get their season up and running

This latest development in the Hammers' ownership saga comes amid the beginning of their mission to make an immediate return to the Premier League following relegation last season.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side picked up their first win of the Championship campaign on Tuesday, beating Wolves 4-2 at the London Stadium.

2 Nuno's West Ham got their first league victory of 2026/27 at the fourth time of asking Credit: Getty

Divine Mukasa bagged a brace for the hosts, with Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also on the scoresheet.



The result, which came after fans had chanted at their previous game for Nuno to be sacked, took West Ham into the top half of table, a point off the play-offs at this early stage of the season.

Next up for the Hammers is another home game against Derby on Saturday.

West Ham dropped back into the second tier after 14 years in the Premier League, their longest top-flight stint since the 1970s.

Their last Championship stint lasted just one season as they were promoted via the play-offs in 2011/12.

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa is left OUT of Liverpool's 25-man Champions League squad in latest blow to Italian - as three injured stars and youngster with only three Premier League appearances make the cut instead
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa's Liverpool career has taken another hit after he was omitted from their UEFA Champions League squad. The Reds have submitted their 25-man squad for Europe's elite club competition which begins on Tuesday. Liverpool begin their quest for an seventh European Cup when they face Atletico Madrid at Anfield on Wednesday night. However, Chiesa will play no part in the tournament after new boss Andoni Iraola chose to not include him for their European campaign. Wataru Endo is another. Chiesa has missed the Merseyside outfit's first two Premier League games of the season due to a muscle injury but when fit will find himself further down their pecking order following the summer signings of fellow forwards Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz. And it is a case of deja-vu for Chiesa, who suffered the same fate from Iraola's predecessor Arne Slot. However, Chiesa was later called-up for their 25-man squad after centre back Giovanni Leoni tore his anterior cruciate ligament. Leoni is one of three Liverpool players currently out injured though that have been selected by Iraola - with Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike completing the trio. Federico Chiesa has been omitted from Liverpool's 25-man squad for the Champions League Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (left) has selected Hugo Ekitike though despite his achilles injury Leoni is set to return to training later this month after nearly a year out, Bradley has been out of action since suffering a knee injury in January and Ekitike has been sidelined since tearing his achilles in April. The inclusion of the injured trio gives Liverpool fans encouragement that they will be involved before the conclusion of the league phase on January 27, 2027. Endo, who like Chiesa has not featured in the opening two matches of the season, has been omitted with James McConnell, 21, preferred among the midfielders. Fellow academy graduates Luke Chambers and Isaac Mabaya are named among 11 defenders on the list. Under UEFA rules, the 25 players named in List A has to include a minimum of eight ‘locally trained’ squad members. Youngsters such as Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni aren’t among them as they can be named on List B given their age. That won't change until they turn 21. Sports.title: Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani
Sports.content:
Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rangers have completed a double deadline day swoop by signing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani.

Kelsy was identified as a priority target when Youssef Chermiti sustained a serious knee injury against Hibernian last month.

The Venezuelan international forward has cost the Ibrox club £9.2million from MLS side Portland Timbers and has signed a four-year deal with an option of a fifth.

The 22-year-old gives manager Derek McInnes another option up front to compete with Lawrence Shankland, Ryan Naderi and Bojan Miovski.

The fee is the second highest in Rangers’ history, second only to the £12m spent on Tore Andre Flo in 2000.

Kelsy came through the ranks of Mineros de Guayana in his home country then moved to Uruguayan outfit Boston River for a short spell before joining Shakhtar Donetsk in January, 2023.

Rangers unveiled the £9million signing of striker Kevin Kelsy from Portland Timbers

The Ibrox club also secured the loan addition of Algerian Badredine Bouanani from Stuttgart

He then joined Portland Timbers in January 2025 after a loan spell at FC Cincinnati.

‘I’ve heard a lot about the club,’ he said. ‘Even when I was younger, I saw the team in Europe. I know what the club means to the fans.

‘I would love to bring some joy to the fans and the club, and score goals to bring amazing moments to the team.

‘I know we have to win all the games and play well, and I’ll be ready for this with my teammates. I’m ready for this new chapter in my life.’

Boss Derek McInnes said: ‘We’re really pleased to welcome Kevin to the club. He’s an exciting player with a lot of attributes, and what really stood out in our conversations is how hungry he is to make an impact.

‘He’ll bring real quality to an area of the pitch we have been keen to strengthen, and his arrival gives us another exciting option going forward.

‘Kevin has a great attitude and a real desire to improve, and we’re looking forward to seeing what he can bring at Rangers.’

Bouanani, 21, has arrived on a year’s loan from Stuttgart, where he operated on the right wing.

The Algerian moved to Germany from Nice in 2025 having played and scored against Rangers for the French club in a European match.

The pair’s arrivals mean Rangers have signed 14 players in this window — either permanently or on loan.

Thelo Aasgaard has gone in the other direction after moving on loan to Anderlecht, while Nico Raskin is staying at the club after Rangers turned down a second bid from Turkish side Besiktas.

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka called upon influencers travelling to the US Open to 'read up' on the sport's rules for spectators after her first-round match was disrupted by a rowdy group in one of Arthur Ashe Stadium's luxury suites.

The four-time Grand Slam champion had been preparing to serve when the chair umpire told off the guests for appearing to stage an impromptu photoshoot, complete with portable lights.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

While Osaka was only half-focused on the specifics of the incident while immersed in defeating her opponent Anastasia Zakharova, discussing what happened on the tournament's showcourt two days later, she suggested that more could be done to ensure that players were not disturbed during matchplay.

'I think obviously, if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport,' she said after her defeat of Katerina Siniakova, which took place on the same court. 'And I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

'I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like first-round match.

Naomi Osaka called for fans new to tennis to learn the sport's etiquette after her match was disrupted by influencers

'Overall I think there is huge positives,' she added, on the topic of influencers more generally. 'You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette.'

Etiquette largely dictates that fans should save conversation and movement for changeovers or set breaks, when the players are at the chairs. But in 2024, the US Open switched to a policy of 'free fan movement', which allows spectators to move during points regardless of on-court action.

Of the incident itself, Osaka said that she had been more bothered by the noise inside the stadium during both her matches - a constant chatter which complements the endless movement - than the flash lights themselves.

'I was going to say today the umpire, she told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet,' she continued.

'I do think in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was, like, people shouting, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too.

'Maybe that's what you were talking about, but I've heard some people say, like, the lights or whatever. I don't really see the lights, because obviously, when you are serving, you're looking at the sun or you're looking at the night lights. It was more the noise.'

Daily Mail Sport contacted the tournament for comment on after Osaka's press conference, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre sharing the following statement: 'The USTA is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport. The US Open is our greatest opportunity to do so, and we welcome newcomers to our event.

'We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court. We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited.

'As a result, we have increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights. The chair umpire also has the ability to address the crowd if and when necessary.'

Sports.title: How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures
Sports.content:
How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Naomi Osaka was not having the easiest time on court. Having battled through a tie-break to edge the first set, she was serving at 4-4 in the second. Then, her concentration snapped.

Up in the luxury suites, a group of influencers were posing for photographs using a bright, portable light. As they milled about the box, unaware of the tension below, their distraction was enough to prompt a warning from the chair umpire. But it took a few moments for the message to filter through. After all, their focus was on getting the perfect shot.

Welcome to the 2026 US Open. Long the envy of the Grand Slams for the late-night energy and glamour that only New York can provide, this year's tournament has been subject to complaints about being overrun with influencers who see the final major of the year as little more than a creative backdrop on social media.

'People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful,' US No 1 Jessica Pegula said when asked about the incident in Osaka's match after her own bow on Arthur Ashe, the tournament's biggest court. 'I think it's gotten a little too much, it feels, this year.'

There's no mystery behind why the US Open has become such a popular destination to tick off for the well-travelled influencer.

'The US Open has evolved from a tennis tournament into one of the most powerful cultural points on the New York calendar,' notes Reece Milner, Senior Strategy Manager at The Goat Agency, a creator and influencer marketing shop. 'It now sits at the intersection of sport, fashion, luxury, hospitality, celebrity, lifestyle and content culture.'

The 'rituals' that appear so frequently on social media feeds that you might be able to play US Open bingo, like enjoying a night match, a Honey Deuce cocktail or $100 COQODAQ chicken nugget-and-caviar box, Milner adds, have only served to crystallise its status.

A group of influencers caught flack for using a portable light to take pictures during Naomi Osaka's match

The US Open has seen a huge rise in popularity in recent years and brands hosting influencers at the tournament in a bid to borrow its cultural clout has risen too

This is no one-way street either, with the US Open well aware of its cultural power outside of tennis as well as within. The tournament has embraced the influencer, this year going as far as to credential 100 content creators, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre noting that in years to come, the number is only going to 'go upwards'.

But those influencers aren't necessarily the problem. Tennis media has evolved to take in TikTok, Instagram, and Substack experts, all invested in growing interest in the game itself. More worthy of skepticism are those who might be spending one night at the Open, making it a race against time to get the perfect picture, action on court be damned.

The US Open has never been Wimbledon, and that's a good thing. The noise of an Arthur Ashe night session makes for pleasing whiplash after the prim-and-proper hush of Centre Court as the tour bounces between the two majors.

But as greater numbers of guests flood into the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center with limited interest in the tennis and more on their feed, the noise levels of ambient chatter, rather than engagement in the match, have caused problems for players.

'On Ashe, you hear everything,' Pegula added. 'Even when there's dead noise, there's still a buzz or a chatter or people talking and eating and laughing and all these different kind of emotions. You really have to do a good job of locking yourself in a bubble when you're out there.'

Of fans on the outdoor courts, French player Adrian Mannarino was more forthright: 'They come in any which way, they move around, they talk. It's the tournament that tolerates this, and I don't know if it's the best idea for the game in general. There's noise coming from everywhere. It's become a bit of a zoo.'

Watching Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz on Arthur Ashe on Wednesday, the noise of the crowd never dipped below 'pub garden'. Since the tournament ushered in 'free fan movement' in 2024 which allows fans to come and go without waiting for changeovers or set breaks, the policy has been followed to the letter, with the lower bowl constantly in motion.

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales

Inside Arthur Ashe Stadium is a constant hum of noise as fans move in their seats during points

That's where most of the chatter comes from too, with the seats in the gods crammed with fans locked in on the action, and quieter during play.

As Alcaraz took the first game after losing his opening set to Jaime Faria, the noise rises to a roar, with the same staticky thickness of a sound machine playing a recording of the ocean at full volume. At 0-15, clearly distracted, the Portuguese player serves a double fault. The chair umpire gives a warning when a fan shouts down from the stands as he's preparing to serve again, but does little to dim the constant conversation.

Nor have those in the suites learned their lesson. Despite the US Open displaying messages around the site telling fans to refrain from using flash or lights to take pictures, Daily Mail Sport spotted flashes going off during Sabalenka's thrashing of Polina Iatcenko.

A statement shared after the Osaka incident placed the responsibility for wrangling misbehaving influencers on the chair umpires, who 'have the ability to address the crowd' when 'infrequent' disruptions occur. On Thursday, an extended second statement responding to Osaka's comments added that the tournament has 'increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights.'

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales. But if the goal is to get more fans into the sport, week-in, week-out, they need great tennis played in a great tennis atmosphere - and inside on the tournament's biggest courts, that can no longer be guaranteed.

Sports.title: FIFA accuse UEFA of a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino and Co after European body threatened legal action as war over failed World Cup sell-off plans escalates
Sports.content:
FIFA says legal applications made by UEFA to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan are part of a 'smear campaign' against the global governing body. UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions. FIFA confirmed last month the plan had been to sell a 20 per cent stake in that company to private investors. The plan was withdrawn by FIFA president Gianni Infantino on August 1 amid opposition from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, the confederation for countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean. That withdrawal has not stopped UEFA pursuing Infantino and other FIFA officials, with UEFA saying documents obtained were intended for use in preparing potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, in filings seen by the Press Association on August 27. The following day, FIFA sought approval to oppose UEFA's request in the Southern District of Florida, a motion which was granted by the court on the next business day, August 31. FIFA has until September 28 to submit a full opposition to that court. A similar motion to oppose was also filed in the Southern District of New York on Tuesday. Documents from FIFA's legal team seen by the Press Association describe UEFA's applications as being 'little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership'. UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin (left) and FIFA counterpart Gianni Infantino are at loggerheads over the latter's failed proposals for World Cup private investor plans FIFA's filing asks the New York court to defer consideration on UEFA's discovery application until the Florida court has ruled on it, or requests that the court permit FIFA permission to oppose UEFA's application no later than September 30. The filing said UEFA's motivation in its opposition to FFE and Infantino was 'to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite'. It added: 'If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces UEFA's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments. 'By raising funds to allow some of FIFA's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad. 'All of this would erode UEFA's dominance over other regions of the world.' UEFA's filing accused Infantino of 'criminal mismanagement' in relation to FFE, and said the proposed sale of a stake for £3.1billion ($4.2bn) in the company was 'a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit'. In a separate statement published last week, UEFA called for an independent external review of the origins of the FFE and said that if Infantino chose to stand for re-election at next year's FIFA Congress, UEFA would 'join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative - one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change'.

Sports.title: Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash
Sports.content:
Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday fuelling hopes that his debut could arrive sooner than expected.

The club-record signing from Freiburg had a knee injury when he joined Villa in July in a deal worth up to £60million, and he has yet to play as he continues his recovery.

Yet Daily Mail Sport understands Manzambi took part in Thursday's session, though it is unclear at this stage whether he would be considered for Saturday's trip to Hull, where Villa will hope to claim their first points of the season after consecutive defeats to Brighton and Arsenal.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on August 31, Emery was cautious about Manzambi, though he hoped the 20-year-old would be able to join in this week.

He said: 'We must be careful. He had an injury and we want his comeback to be clear and strong, with no risk.

'Progressively, he is working individually and is starting collectively with the group this week.'

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday as he stepped up his recovery

After losing key members of the team who lifted the Europa League and qualified for the Champions League last term, Villa have tried to rebuild by making 11 signings. Emery has also brought forward Brian Madjo and midfielder George Hemmings into the first-team group.

Morgan Rogers moved to Chelsea this summer for a record £117m, with Emi Martinez also making the switch to Stamford Bridge. Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa also departed in a summer of huge change at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues in fits of laughter following his thoughts about the statistic 'Expected Goals' (xG).

Speaking on the latest episode of the show, brought to you by Disney+, the former Manchester United captain expressed why he believes that particular stat - which measures the probability that a given shot will result in a goal - is irrelevant.

Sitting alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott and Ian Wright, Keane started his point animatedly with: 'Do you know what that stat is?

'Years ago, when you'd go to a nightclub back in the day, and you'd chat to a girl all night, but you go home by yourself. What's your xG?'

Keane's quip left Neville, Carragher, Scott and Wright in stitches. Neville then replied self-depreciatingly: 'Roy, I kept clean sheets!'

A smirking Roy said: 'I'm sure you did, yeah!'

xG explained the Roy Keane way! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/qJOS705noc — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 3, 2026

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues laughing with his views on Expected Goals (xG)

Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher were in hysterics after Keane compared it to nightclubs

During the show, the quintet discussed the closing of the summer transfer window - following Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

Among the clubs discussed was Liverpool - with Carragher believing Reds boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right back permanently.

Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot.

Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far.

With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer.

Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola.

Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back

'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said.

'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that.

'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there.

'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Sports.title: David Sullivan to INCREASE stake in West Ham despite sexual misconduct allegations - with Royal Mail chief to become largest shareholder in huge blow to Amanda Staveley
Sports.content:
David Sullivan to INCREASE stake in West Ham despite sexual misconduct allegations - with Royal Mail chief to become largest shareholder in huge blow to Amanda Staveley

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the largest shareholder at West Ham United – with David Sullivan also increasing his stake in the club.

In a move that would deliver a major blow to Amanda Staveley, who had reached an initial agreement to buy the Gold family’s 25.1 per cent stake in the Championship outfit, Czech billionaire Kretinsky is thought to have exercised pre-emption rights.

It means Kretinsky, along with the other existing shareholders, will instead split the Golds' holding, leaving former Newcastle United director Staveley in the cold.

Terms of the deal are yet to be disclosed however, it is understood that, as a result, Royal Mail owner Kretinsky will up his stake from 27 to 46 per cent, with Sullivan – who stood down as joint-chairman in June in the wake of serious allegations that he abused his power by preying on women for sex – increasing his holding from 38.8 per cent to 40 per cent. American investor Tripp Smith would expand his share from 8 to 11 per cent, with the remaining shareholders rising from 1.1 to 3 per cent.

Former West Ham joint-chairman David Sullivan is set to increase his stake in the club

Sullivan, 77, ‘categorically’ denies the claims against him. He is banned from having one-to-one contact or direct access to the Hammers women’s and youth teams following a historical complaint to the FA. The Independent Football Regulator said it would seek ‘urgent information’ regarding the allegations from Sullivan, and also contacted Essex Police.

West Ham have been contacted for comment. Staveley had offered £150m for the Gold stake, which some viewed as the first step towards a full takeover.

Sports.title: FIFA accuse UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
FIFA accuse UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino

FIFA and UEFA's bitter public spat has taken another turn with the latter accused of launching a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino following his plot to sell World Cup shares

View 2 Images Aleksandr Ceferin and Gianni Infantino do not see eye to eye (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA has been accused of running a "smear campaign" against Gianni Infantino by FIFA following the former's attempt to launch legal action over a failed plot to sell shares in the World Cup.

‌



Infantino was heavily criticised after unveiling a scheme to sell off shares in future FIFA tournaments to private investors, with UEFA's nations even threatening to boycott World Cups if the proposals were put into action.

‌



The 56-year-old eventually rowed back on the proposals but has been subjected to calls for his resignation, while it emerged last week that UEFA are preparing a criminal file against Infantino.

‌



They filed legal papers in the United States requesting the release of evidence and documents from FIFA. But they have responded with court filings of their own in which they accused UEFA of "a smear campaign against it and its leadership".

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The governing body also claims that UEFA's argument suffers from "legal deficiencies". According to BBC Sport, the filings say: "UEFA seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that UEFA admittedly lacks the authority to initiate. Despite that threshold problem, UEFA asks this court to authorise sweeping discovery about the FFE."

‌



FIFA went on to stress that it had "made clear" the creation of FFE (Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme) was "only a proposal" and would not have proceeded without overwhelming support.

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, Uefa issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership," FIFA wrote.

In their court filing, UEFA described the creation of FFE as "a vehicle for Infantino and a small circle to acquire a permanent stake and otherwise profit from Fifa’s most valuable assets."

‌



View 2 Images Infantino's position has come under scrutiny in recent weeks (Image: Zac Goodwin/PA Wire)

The fallout of the proposals have left the two governing bodies at war, although UEFA has now dropped the threat of its nations boycotting future World Cup tournaments.

UEFA are also pushing for Joshua Kushner, a venture capitalist and the son-in-law of Donald Trump who was set to be the lead investor in FFE, for a testimony.

Article continues below

Kushner apologised for the abandoned venture on Sunday, saying: "While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to… had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

Sports.title: Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad after botched Everton move
Sports.content:
Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad after botched Everton move

Richarlison is set to be frozen out at Tottenham unless he is able to agree a transfer overseas after a potential return to the striker's former club Everton collapsed

View 2 Images Richarlison has omitted from Tottenham's Premier League squad (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Richarlison has not been included in Tottenham's squad for the Premier League this season, with the striker now free to explore a move abroad.

‌



Spurs have spent heavily this summer to overhaul their squad after two disastrous Premier League campaigns, with the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Savio all signing for significant transfer fees. Omar Marmoush has also arrived in attack on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent next summer, nudging Richarlison further down the pecking order.

‌



It seemed as though a return to the Brazilian's former club, Everton, was in the offing in the final knockings of the transfer window with Tottenham in turn lining up a move for Iliman Ndiaye.

‌



But both deals collapsed with Ndiaye subsequently joining Manchester City - and Richarlison now faces being left out in the cold if he remains in north London.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It's been confirmed that the 29-year-old has been omitted from Spurs squad, meaning he is unable to feature in Premier League games for the first half of the season.

‌



One option for the former Watford striker is a move overseas with several international transfer windows still open. Turkey is one such option and there has been interest in Richarlison's services from Trabzonspor, who have already seen a bid for his services rebuffed by Tottenham. Saudi Pro League clubs can also still sign players and could offer Richarlison a career lifeline.

The player, who was left out of the Tottenham squad which lost 2-0 against Newcastle on Saturday, has just one year remaining on his current contract.

A return to Everton, where he enjoyed a successful four year spell before moving to Spurs, looked to tick all the boxes in the final hours of the transfer window. However, Richarlison took to social media to explain why a move would not go through.

‌



View 2 Images Richarlison was a huge hit at Everton before joining Spurs but a potential return to Merseyside collapsed (Image: Getty Images )

“After everything I’ve been through in the last few years, I’ve decided that never again will anyone decide my future for me,” he wrote. “I went through a lot of bad things, and almost all of them happened because decisions were made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation — none of that scares me. I’ve been through far worse, believe me.

“I always made it clear, on every occasion, that if I were to leave for another place, it would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it… just as I didn’t when everything here was falling apart and they needed me. I stayed and gave my life to it.

Article continues below

“So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for everyone who has worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

Sports.title: Constitution Hill feared for "lumpy six-figure payout" by bookie as star goes to Kempton
Sports.content:
Constitution Hill feared for "lumpy six-figure payout" by bookie as star goes to Kempton

The ex-champion hurdler is back on the track for the first time in 164 days on Saturday. Nicky Henderson's trainee will have Billy Loughnane in the saddle, who has a 15-win lead in the jockeys' championship

View 2 Images Constitution Hill (Image: Getty Images)

One bookmaker is fearing a "lumpy six-figure payout" as former jumping star Constitution Hill gets back on track at Kempton Park.

‌



The nine-year-old gelding is 2-2 in Flat races and is set to take a big rise in class for the Group Three September Stakes (2.50pm) on Saturday.

‌



Over 1m 4f, the contest will have seven runners in total, including Coral-Eclipse fifth Gethin and Tornado Alert, a Group One scorer in Germany.

‌



Race sponsors William Hill offered odds of 12-1 about Constitution Hill at the start of the week and by the declaration stage his price had tumbled to 5-1.

"We’re going to need some of the established Flat performers to oblige if we’re to dodge a lumpy six-figure payout.

Sports.title: Arsenal deal for Bruno Guimaraes rated one out of 10 in brutal transfer ranking
Sports.content:
Arsenal deal for Bruno Guimaraes rated one out of 10 in brutal transfer ranking

Bruno Guimaraes has been heavily criticised for his decision to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal

View Image Bruno Guimaraes has been slammed for his decision to join Arsenal

Bruno Guimaraes' move from Newcastle United to Arsenal has been slammed with a 1/10 rating by former Magpies defender Steven Taylor, who says he is baffled by the Brazilian's decision to join the Premier League champions. Taylor, now head coach of UAE side Desert Falcon, questioned why Guimaraes chose to leave a project he had been central to on Tyneside.

‌



Arsenal agreed a £75million deal with Newcastle for the former Lyon midfielder, who has signed a four‑year contract at the Emirates. Guimaraes spent four seasons at St James' Park before opting to move on, with Newcastle offloading several key players, including Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, less than a year after Alexander Isak’s departure.

‌



"He's made the worst decision," Taylor told Stadium Astro. "I don't understand why he'd leave Newcastle to go to Arsenal, but he made his decision. I'd give that transfer 1/10.

‌



"I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this," Guimaraes said after signing for the Gunners. "I want to win trophies.

"I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start."

Taylor was equally scathing about Sandro Tonali following the midfielder’s £100million switch to Tottenham, Arsenal’s north London rivals. The Italian has already faced his former club this season, with Spurs falling to a 2–0 defeat against Newcastle in the second Premier League fixture.

‌



The former defender said: "He tried too hard and the Newcastle fans gave him hell and the players as well. I'm sure there were a few things said on the pitch with former players getting into as well.

"He's usually a problem to play against, but against Newcastle he didn't cause any."

‌



Taylor believes both players are in for a rough reception if they return to St James' Park later in the campaign. Arsenal head to the north east in November, with Tottenham following in April.

Former Newcastle favourite Isak was met with a torrent of jeers on the opening day of the season after his acrimonious exit in 2025, and the Swede struggled to make any impact against his old club.

Taylor added: "It's always good and the manager will be saying: 'Let's get into them'. You want to make sure the tackles are going in. You want to upset them and you know their weaknesses."
