World.title: Fire During C-Section at Bulovka Hospital Leaves Woman Seriously Burned
World.content:
A woman suffered serious burns during an emergency cesarean section at Prague’s Bulovka Hospital on Aug. 25, hospital spokeswoman Eva Stolejda Libigerová said.

The cesarean was performed because of an acute obstetric complication. The woman’s condition is now stable and she does not require intensive care, the hospital said. She is recovering in a standard ward with her newborn.



The hospital is investigating the incident as part of its internal procedures for reviewing patient safety and the quality of medical care. It said it would take appropriate measures once the investigation is complete.

Fire broke out during surgery

According to information obtained about the incident, medical staff were attempting to control bleeding toward the end of the operation when a fire broke out involving a surgical device.

The device was reportedly being used shortly after the patient’s skin had been treated with a disinfectant.

The woman suffered second- and third-degree burns to her inner thighs, sides, lower abdomen and genital area, according to the available information.

Two days after the operation, she was transferred to the Burns Medicine Clinic at University Hospital Královské Vinohrady for treatment. She was later returned to Bulovka Hospital’s postpartum ward.

The circumstances surrounding the fire, including how it started and whether established safety procedures were followed, are being examined by the hospital.

Previous incident at Bulovka maternity clinic

The hospital’s gynecology and obstetrics clinic was also the site of a serious medical error in March 2024.

In that case, staff mistakenly identified two patients of Asian origin. A pregnant woman who had arrived for a routine examination was incorrectly subjected to a curettage procedure, resulting in the loss of her pregnancy.

An internal investigation concluded that two employees had violated established procedures and internal rules. The hospital subsequently ended its cooperation with one of them.

Police also investigated the case on suspicion of negligent bodily harm but ultimately brought no charges.

The woman later reached a settlement with the hospital worth 2.3 million Czech crowns. One of the employees involved lost her job.

World.title: Ambiente to Open Its 35th Prague Establishment This September
World.content:
Restaurant group Ambiente is preparing to open its 35th establishment, with a second location of its Pult beer concept set to launch in Prague’s Holešovice district in mid-September.

The new venue will be located on Tusarova Street and will follow the concept of Pult in Prague 1, which opened in the Celnice building in 2021.



While both locations will focus on Czech lager, the new Holešovice branch will introduce a different food concept and its own selection of beers.

The original venue serves beers from six breweries, with an emphasis on precise storage, serving and temperature control.

A different approach to food

Food will be one of the main differences between the two Pult locations.

The original Pult in Celnice focuses largely on smaller dishes and snacks. The Holešovice restaurant will instead offer a more substantial menu designed specifically to accompany beer.

The menu is expected to focus heavily on Czech beef, including several versions of steak tartare and steaks. Unlike many restaurants where the kitchen closes earlier than the bar, the new Pult plans to serve food until closing at 1 a.m.

The restaurant will have space for around 130 guests.

Another new destination for Holešovice

The opening comes as Holešovice continues to attract new restaurants, cafés and cultural venues. The area has become home to places including Vnitroblock, Mexická, Slice Slice Baby, Eatery, Ema, Typika, Osada and Polepšovna.

Ambiente itself has expanded its presence in Holešovice this year. At the Holešovice Market, the group has opened a second location of its Myšák confectionery and Naše maso butcher shop, as well as Skô, a Slovak-focused restaurant concept.

World.title: 7 Autumn Bike Trips to Take Around Czechia
World.content:
With cooler temperatures and autumn colours arriving, September and October are among the best months for cycling in Czechia.

The country’s extensive network of marked trails makes it easy to plan anything from a relaxed day trip to a multi-day adventure.

Here are seven routes worth considering this autumn.



1. Prague–Mělník–Litoměřice

One of the easiest options for Prague residents is to head north along the Elbe. The route passes through Mělník, known for its vineyards and historic centre, before continuing towards Litoměřice.

Along the way, cyclists can see Roudnice Chateau, Mount Říp and the historic fortress town of Terezín. Mělník is particularly appealing in September, when its wine season is in full swing.

2. Znojmo Wine Route

For a combination of cycling and wine, South Moravia is hard to beat in autumn. The 63-kilometre Znojmo Wine Route connects vineyards and villages around Znojmo and is suitable for cyclists of different abilities.

September and October are also the region’s main wine-harvest season, with numerous wine and burčák events taking place.

3. Mikulov and Pálava

The Mikulov Wine Trail offers another relaxed way to explore South Moravia. The route takes cyclists through vineyards and the countryside around Mikulov, with the Pálava hills providing one of the region’s most distinctive landscapes.

It is particularly attractive in September, when the annual Pálava Wine Festival takes place.

4. Singltrek pod Smrkem

If road cycling isn’t your thing, head towards Liberec. Singltrek pod Smrkem has more than 60 kilometres of purpose-built mountain-bike trails, ranging from easier sections for beginners to more challenging routes.

The surrounding Jizera Mountains also make it a good destination for a weekend trip.

5. Bečva Cycling Trail

The almost 160-kilometre Bečva Cycling Trail follows the Bečva River across Moravia. The route can be completed over several days and is largely downhill when ridden from the river’s source towards its confluence with the Morava.

Highlights along the way include Helfštýn Castle, the Zbrašovské Aragonite Caves and the open-air museum in Rožnov pod Radhoštěm.

6. Ploučnice Cycle Path

The nearly 100-kilometre Ploučnice Cycle Path runs from the river’s source near Ještěd to Děčín. It passes through Česká Lípa, the Ralsko area and the Kokořínsko-Máchův kraj landscape before reaching the Elbe.

7. Prague–Vienna Greenway

For a more ambitious trip, the Prague–Vienna Greenway stretches 368 kilometres between the two capitals. The route passes through historic towns, castles and monasteries, including Tábor, Znojmo and Mikulov.

It takes roughly a week to complete with stops, making it better suited to a longer autumn holiday than a weekend ride.

World.title: How to Buy TikTok Followers Without Risking Your Account
World.content:
Building a TikTok audience from zero can be frustrating. Even well-produced videos may struggle to attract attention when an account has only a handful of followers.

This slow beginning encourages some creators and businesses to purchase followers in the hope of making their profiles appear more established. Follower count can influence first impressions. When visitors discover a profile with an existing audience, they may be more willing to watch its videos, explore older content, or follow the account themselves. However, purchased followers cannot replace engaging videos or genuine interaction. Low-quality services may also deliver inactive accounts that disappear quickly or create an unnatural gap between follower numbers and actual engagement. Anyone considering this approach should understand how follower services operate, what they can realistically provide, and which warning signs suggest that a seller should be avoided.

Why Creators Purchase TikTok Followers

New accounts frequently face a credibility problem. Viewers have little information to judge whether the creator is worth following, so the visible follower count becomes one of several signals they use to make that decision. A larger audience can make a profile appear more established. This is particularly relevant for businesses, influencers, musicians, and other new TikTok creators trying to build authority in a competitive category. Some creators also purchase TikTok followers to reach eligibility thresholds for particular TikTok features. TikTok commonly applies age, location, and follower requirements to features such as LIVE, although the exact conditions may differ between markets and can change over time. The important distinction is that purchased followers mainly affect appearance. They may strengthen the profile’s initial social proof, but they do not guarantee greater reach, more sales, or stronger engagement.

What Purchased Followers Can and Cannot Do

Follower count is visible to anyone who visits a TikTok profile, which means it can shape the visitor’s first impression. A profile with several thousand followers may look more credible than an otherwise similar account with fewer than 100. TikTok’s recommendation system, however, evaluates much more than audience size. Signals such as watch time, completion rate, rewatches, shares, comments, saves, and viewer satisfaction are generally more important when determining whether a video should reach a wider audience. This creates a potential problem. If an account displays 30,000 followers but its videos consistently receive only a few dozen views, the imbalance may look unnatural to both TikTok and real visitors. Brands evaluating the creator for a partnership may notice the same discrepancy. Purchased followers should therefore be understood as a limited form of social proof. They cannot:

Make weak videos more entertaining

Guarantee placement on the For You feed

Produce meaningful comments or conversations

Create loyal customers

Replace a consistent publishing strategy

Automatically generate revenue

The greatest risk comes from purchasing followers that are obviously automated, inactive, or created only to inflate account statistics. These profiles add little value and may be removed during platform cleanups.

How to Evaluate a TikTok Follower Provider

The market contains everything from established social media marketing platforms to temporary websites selling automated accounts. A professional design alone does not prove that a service is dependable, so each provider should be evaluated carefully. Platforms such as SocialWick offer clearly defined TikTok packages and a conventional ordering process. Regardless of which company is being considered, several basic checks should be completed before placing an order.

Check the Website’s Security

A provider should use HTTPS encryption to protect information submitted through its website. This can usually be confirmed by checking for the padlock symbol beside the address in the browser. Secure payment methods are equally important. Credit cards and reputable payment processors normally offer better consumer protection than cryptocurrency transfers, gift cards, or other payment methods that are difficult to reverse.

Never Provide a TikTok Password

A follower delivery service generally needs only the public username or a link to the TikTok profile. It should not require the account password, email login, recovery code, or two-factor authentication details. Requests for private credentials are a serious warning sign. Sharing this information could allow an unknown company to access the account, change its settings, publish content, or lock out the owner.

Review the Delivery Time

Instant delivery may sound convenient, but an enormous follower increase within minutes can look unnatural. A newer account is unlikely to gain tens of thousands of followers suddenly without a viral video or another clear reason. More credible providers commonly offer gradual delivery. This spreads the order across several hours or days and makes it easier to monitor the quality of the accounts being added.

Understand the Package Quality

Follower packages are often divided into labels such as standard, high quality, active, real, or premium. These terms are not standardized, so they can mean different things on different websites. A higher-priced package may include accounts with profile photos, usernames, existing posts, or more complete activity histories. Cheaper options frequently consist of empty or inactive profiles. Before paying extra for a so-called premium tier, buyers should read the description carefully and determine what the seller is actually promising. Independent comparisons of TikTok follower providers and package quality may provide additional context, but customer reviews and seller claims should still be treated cautiously.

Look for Accessible Customer Support

A legitimate business should provide a clear way to request assistance. Live chat, email support, or a functioning contact form gives customers somewhere to report missing followers, delayed orders, or payment problems. Support availability does not automatically prove that a provider is trustworthy. However, a website with no contact information, unanswered messages, and no stated resolution process presents a much greater risk.

Warning Signs That Should Not Be Ignored

Very low pricing is one of the most common signs of poor-quality delivery. Maintaining accounts that look authentic requires more resources than operating a large collection of disposable bots. Consequently, offers promising thousands of “real and active” followers for a few cents are unlikely to match their description. Other warning signs include:

Requests for passwords or security codes

Guaranteed viral results

Promises of automatic monetization

No terms of service or privacy policy

Prices far below comparable providers

Only irreversible payment methods

Broken pages or copied website content

No delivery estimate

No refund or replacement policy

Large numbers of identical customer reviews

Claims of guaranteed engagement also deserve scrutiny. No external provider can honestly promise that purchased followers will watch every video or become paying customers.

Why a Refill Policy Matters

Follower losses can occur after an order is completed. TikTok may remove suspicious accounts, users may deactivate their profiles, or low-quality followers may simply disappear. A refill policy allows customers to request replacements when the follower count drops within a specified period. Depending on the provider, this protection may last for several days or a month. The conditions should be reviewed before checkout. Some companies refill only when the loss exceeds a minimum amount, while others exclude certain packages. Buyers should also check whether the replacement is automatic or must be requested manually. A refill guarantee cannot eliminate every risk, but it shows that the provider has at least acknowledged the possibility of follower loss and established a process for addressing it.

Avoid Unnatural Growth Patterns

Sudden, unexplained growth can draw unwanted attention. An account that gains 10,000 followers overnight without publishing anything new may appear suspicious, particularly if its views and interactions remain unchanged. Gradual delivery is generally less disruptive than receiving an entire order immediately. However, spreading out a purchase should not be treated as a method for bypassing TikTok’s enforcement systems. Buying followers may still conflict with platform rules, and no delivery method can guarantee that an account will avoid restrictions or removals.

Creators who choose to purchase followers should keep the order proportionate to the profile’s existing size. Adding a modest number to an active account is less conspicuous than transforming a nearly empty profile into a large one overnight. Content should also continue to be published consistently. A larger number beneath the profile image will have little effect if visitors arrive and find outdated, irrelevant, or poorly produced videos.

Keep Engagement and Follower Numbers Balanced

Follower count is only one part of a TikTok profile. Views, likes, comments, shares, and posting frequency provide a broader picture of its actual performance. If follower growth significantly outpaces every other metric, the account may lose credibility. A profile with 20,000 followers and almost no interaction may look less trustworthy than one with 2,000 followers and an active community. Maintaining a reasonable balance requires genuine content work. Creators should continue to:

Publish videos on a consistent schedule

Capture attention within the opening seconds

Respond to real comments

Participate in relevant trends

Use searchable captions and keywords

Test different formats and video lengths

Review analytics to identify strong topics

Collaborate with creators in the same niche

These activities provide TikTok with behavioral signals that purchased followers cannot produce.

Turning Social Proof Into Organic Growth

The most practical reason to purchase followers is to improve the profile’s initial presentation. If that stronger appearance encourages more people to explore the content, it may indirectly support organic growth. This effect depends entirely on what visitors find after opening the profile. A clear bio, recognizable niche, strong video covers, and a useful collection of content can convert curiosity into a genuine follow. An inflated number without quality content is unlikely to accomplish the same result. Creators should prepare their profiles before purchasing anything. A complete profile should include:

A memorable username

A clear profile image

A concise description of the account

Several high-quality published videos

Pinned content that represents the creator’s best work

A consistent subject or visual identity

An appropriate call to action

Purchased followers may bring the profile closer to the starting line, but the content determines whether real viewers remain interested.

Final Considerations Before Buying TikTok Followers

Buying TikTok followers can improve the visible size of an account, but it should never be confused with building a real community. The number may influence first impressions, yet it cannot reproduce the value of genuine viewers who regularly interact with the content. Anyone considering a purchase should choose a provider carefully, avoid sharing login information, use protected payment methods, read the refill conditions, and remain skeptical of unrealistic guarantees. It is also important to recognize that follower purchases may violate TikTok’s rules and could lead to removals or other account consequences. The strongest TikTok profiles combine credibility with content that earns attention. Purchased followers may change how a profile looks, but sustainable growth still depends on originality, consistency, audience understanding, and videos that people genuinely want to watch.

World.title: Vinohrady’s Americká Street Block Party Returns on September 12
World.content:
Americká and Záhřebská streets in Prague’s Vinohrady will turn into a pedestrian festival zone on Saturday, September 12, for the 15th edition of Zažít Americkou jinak.

From 10:30 AM to 9:30 PM, the streets will host a full-day programme of live music, dance, workshops, design, food and activities for children. The festival is free to attend.

A major part of this year’s programme will focus on Mexico and Latin American culture, including a celebration of Mexican Independence Day.



The main programme will take place on the La Calle Mexicana Stage, hosted by DJs Roxana Velasco and José. Visitors can look forward to performances by Studio Anyo, traditional Mexican music, a piñata, a dance workshop and appearances by Mexican musicians Razcarmelo and Andrea Viruega.

One of the highlights will be El Grito, the traditional ceremony marking Mexico’s Independence Day. The event has become an annual gathering point for the Mexican community in Czechia and festival visitors.

The programme will also feature Mariachi Azteca de Praga, described as the first authentic mariachi band based in the Czech Republic.

The evening will continue with international acts including Faustina Calavera, a ten-member band from Wrocław combining Latin American cumbia, Balkan brass and ska, followed by ONIXIA, an Argentine singer, dancer and songwriter based in Berlin who blends electronic music with Latin American rhythms.

More Space to Relax

This year’s festival will also feature an expanded chill-out zone at the intersection of Americká and Jana Masaryka streets, with seating, workshops and space to meet friends and neighbours.

Music will also be played at two additional locations. The Burza #4 Stage will return by the fountain at the corner of Americká and Záhřebská streets, while another stage on Záhřebská Street will focus on world and house music.

MINT Market, Food and Local Businesses

The festival will once again include MINT Market, bringing together dozens of Czech designers, independent makers and creators from Latin America. Visitors can browse fashion, jewellery, illustrations, ceramics, natural cosmetics and other handmade products.

Food will be another major part of the day, with Mexican, Latin American and international cuisine, street food and special offers from cafés, restaurants and other local businesses.

During the festival, Americká and Záhřebská streets will be closed to traffic and parking.

World.title: New Pharmacy Partnership Makes Prescription Drugs Easier for Foreigners in Czechia
World.content:
Foreigners from outside the EU insured with Maxima pojišťovna can now collect prescription medicines at selected pharmacies without paying upfront.

The Czech insurer has expanded its network of partner pharmacies through a new agreement with LÉKÁRNA U MUZEA in Prague 1.

Under the arrangement, the pharmacy and insurer handle the reimbursement directly, bringing the process closer to the system used by patients covered by Czech public health insurance.



The change is aimed at simplifying access to medicines for foreigners, who can face difficulties navigating the Czech healthcare system and understanding the costs associated with medical treatment.

According to figures cited by the insurer, nearly 900,000 people from non-EU countries have been living in the Czech Republic on a long-term basis. They account for about 8.2 percent of the country’s population.

How the new system works

Previously, foreign clients with commercial health insurance could be required to pay for prescribed medicines at the pharmacy and then submit the receipts to their insurer for reimbursement.

Under the new arrangement, this step is eliminated. Eligible Maxima clients can collect their prescribed medicines through the partner pharmacy, while the financial settlement takes place directly between the pharmacy and the insurance company.

The model has already been operating for more than a year at the pharmacy operated by Maxima’s healthcare partner Innova Healthcare at the Hůrka Polyclinic in Prague.

The data also highlights some of the most common medical needs among patients visiting the participating clinics. More than 63 percent of patients seen by general practitioners, pediatricians and gynecologists were prescribed antibiotics.

More than 37 percent required treatment for sideropenic anemia, or iron deficiency, while 20 percent received prescriptions for blood-thinning medication following injuries.

The pharmacy in Prague 1 will also stock medical equipment and rehabilitation aids. Its range includes orthoses, crutches, wheelchairs and products for convalescence, rehabilitation and everyday healthcare.

Maxima says it intends to expand the direct-settlement model to additional partner pharmacies in the future.

World.title: Dozens of Hot Air Balloons to Fill Czech Skies During September Festival
World.content:
Dozens of hot air balloons are expected to take to the skies over eastern Bohemia this week as the Balonové Nebe festival returns to Hradec Králové, Jaroměř and nearby areas.

The five-day event will run from Wednesday, September 2, through Sunday, September 6, with a program combining competitive balloon flights, mass launches and evening shows. All public events are free to attend.

Weather will play a major role in the festival schedule. Balloon flights can only take place under suitable conditions, meaning launch sites and departure times may change at short notice.



Organizers say the exact location of each flight will depend mainly on wind direction and other weather conditions. Planned flights may also be postponed or cancelled if conditions are unsuitable.

The festival has established itself as one of the country’s major hot air balloon gatherings. Last year’s event set a Czech record when 81 balloons flew into the sky at the same time.

The 2026 edition will once again feature morning competitions, during which pilots will complete a series of tasks while large groups of balloons rise over the region.

Evening programs will offer a different spectacle, with balloon shows planned for spectators. The precise locations of these events will be announced according to the weather forecast and flying conditions.

Visitors planning to attend are advised to check the festival’s official website before setting out. The organizers will publish the latest information about launch locations, times and any changes to the schedule there.

World.title: VIDEO: Golden STARLUX Lands in Prague for the First Time
World.content:
A golden Airbus A350-1000 operated by Taiwan’s STARLUX Airlines landed at Václav Havel Airport Prague for the first time on Tuesday, September 1.

The aircraft, registered as B-58554, carries the special AIRSORAYAMA Gold livery created in collaboration with Japanese artist Hajime Sorayama.

Prague is one of only three destinations where STARLUX plans to operate the specially designed aircraft on a regular basis, alongside Tokyo and Phoenix.



The arrival marks another step in the expansion of STARLUX’s new direct connection between Prague and Taipei.

The airline launched the route on August 1, initially using the smaller Airbus A350-900. From September, the carrier has switched to the larger A350-1000, which can carry up to 350 passengers in four travel classes.

STARLUX, Airbus and paint manufacturer Mankiewicz developed a multilayer coating using mica particles to create the metallic effect while meeting aviation safety requirements.

Increasing capacity on Prague route

STARLUX launched Prague as its first European destination on August 1, connecting the Czech capital directly with Taipei three times a week. The service currently operates on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays.

Flight JX101 leaves Taipei at 12:10 a.m. and arrives in Prague at 8:35 a.m. The return flight, JX102, departs Prague at 10:35 a.m. and arrives in Taipei at 7:55 a.m. the following day.

The switch to the A350-1000 increases the available capacity on the route. The aircraft has four travel classes, including First Class, Business Class, Premium Economy and Economy.

An additional Monday flight is scheduled to operate from October through November, bringing the route to four flights per week during that period.

World.title: Ukraine makes major gesture towards Hungary, officially condemning Soviet atrocities against Transcarpathian Hungarians
World.content:
Ukraine’s parliament has made an important gesture towards Hungary by officially recognising and condemning crimes committed by the Soviet military administration in Transcarpathia between 1944 and 1946.

The Verkhovna Rada adopted the declaration unanimously, with 261 MPs voting in favour, with no votes against and no abstentions.

The resolution specifically recognises the mass repression suffered by the region’s Hungarian civilian population, including the notorious ‘malenky robot’, during which thousands of civilians were deported to labour camps in the Soviet Union, the Hungarian Democratic Alliance in Ukraine reported.

The decision comes at a particularly sensitive time in Hungarian-Ukrainian relations, as Hungary continues to block certain steps in Ukraine’s EU accession process and has repeatedly called on Kyiv to address the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia.

If you missed it: FM Anita Orbán shares what Hungary expects from Ukraine in order for the government to withdraw its veto

Ukraine officially condemns Soviet-era crimes

According to the declaration, following the withdrawal of Hungarian and German forces in autumn 1944, Transcarpathia immediately came under the control of the Soviet military administration.

With the involvement of the Soviet secret police organisations NKVD and SMERSH, the authorities carried out mass and unlawful arrests of civilian men aged between 18 and 50 under the pretext of mobilisation for labour camps.

The Ukrainian parliament states that thousands of peaceful residents of Transcarpathia were deported to the Gulag system without a court ruling. The declaration describes these actions as crimes committed by the communist totalitarian regime.

The ‘malenky robot’ is recognised as a crime

One of the most significant elements of the resolution is Ukraine’s official recognition of the repression of the region’s Hungarian civilian population.

The declaration specifically mentions the ‘malenky robot’, or ‘little work’, and recognises the mass repression of ethnic Hungarians between 1944 and 1946 as a crime committed by the communist totalitarian regime.

The document also condemns the repression suffered by Transcarpathia’s ethnic German population during the same period. The Ukrainian parliament says that, as a democratic state committed to the rule of law and opposed to all forms of totalitarianism, Ukraine has a moral duty to officially acknowledge these historical crimes.

Memorials and educational programmes planned

The declaration goes beyond simply acknowledging the historical events. Ukraine also considers it a moral obligation to honour the victims of Soviet repression in Transcarpathia, including through the installation of memorial plaques. The document also calls for scientific research and educational programmes concerning the persecution, while promising greater public access to relevant archival materials.

What was the ‘malenky robot’?

The term ‘malenky robot’, meaning ‘little work’, is widely used to describe the mass deportation of Hungarians and Germans from Transcarpathia by Soviet authorities after the Second World War. In autumn 1944, civilian men were often rounded up under the pretext of being taken away for short-term labour. Many, however, were subsequently deported to labour camps across the Soviet Union.

Large numbers never returned home. The new parliamentary declaration is therefore significant because the Ukrainian state has now formally recognised and condemned these events in an official parliamentary document.

Decision comes amid tensions over Ukraine’s EU accession

The Ukrainian parliament’s move comes as relations between Kyiv and Budapest remain strained. On Thursday, it emerged that Ukraine’s EU accession process was still facing obstacles because Hungary continues to block the screening reports linked to the second and third negotiating clusters.

The Hungarian government has repeatedly stated that it does not support Ukraine’s accelerated accession to the European Union and expects Kyiv to implement an agreement concerning the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia.

Against this backdrop, the Ukrainian parliament’s decision can be seen as a significant political and symbolic gesture towards Budapest, even though it does not resolve all of the outstanding disputes between the two countries.

World.title: Disturbing: Hungarian couple abuses and starves woman to death
World.content:
A 34-year-old vulnerable woman was held as a slave, forced to work and repeatedly abused before dying from extreme neglect, prosecutors say.

A Hungarian couple convicted of abusing and starving a vulnerable 34-year-old woman to death could face significantly harsher sentences after prosecutors appealed the first-instance verdict.

The couple, who were convicted of causing death by bodily harm, human trafficking and forced labour, were sentenced by the Nyíregyháza Regional Court to 14 and 10 years in prison respectively.

The Debrecen Appellate Chief Prosecutor’s Office has now called for the sentences to be increased and for the case to be reclassified as murder committed with particular cruelty. Prosecutors are seeking a life sentence for the male defendant and a substantially longer sentence for his wife.

Woman promised accommodation and care

According to the prosecution, the couple took the 34-year-old woman into their home in the summer of 2023. The woman was in a vulnerable situation and had reportedly been promised accommodation and care in exchange for helping with household chores.

Instead, prosecutors say, the couple kept her locked inside, forced her to work and provided her with very little food. She was also allegedly subjected to regular physical abuse, including being beaten by hand and with a rolling pin and repeatedly attacked with a stun device.

The prolonged abuse and starvation left the woman severely weakened and emaciated. On the morning of 28 April 2024, she reportedly failed to get up and was no longer communicating.

Couple failed to seek medical help

Rather than calling for medical assistance, the couple allegedly decided to transport the woman towards Budapest. According to the prosecution, their son and his partner helped place the woman in a car before the journey began.

During the trip, the couple realised that she had died. They subsequently left the motorway and allegedly abandoned her body, together with her identity card and bank card, in the car park of an apartment building.

The woman’s body was later discovered by children who happened to be passing by.

First-instance court handed down prison sentences

The Nyíregyháza Regional Court found both defendants guilty of causing death by bodily harm, human trafficking and forced labour. The man was sentenced to 14 years in prison, while his wife received a 10-year prison sentence.

Both the defendants and their lawyers appealed against the ruling. They are seeking an acquittal as their primary request, or alternatively a different legal classification and a reduction in their sentences. The prosecution, meanwhile, is seeking significantly harsher punishment.

Prosecutors seek life imprisonment

The Debrecen Appellate Chief Prosecutor’s Office argues that the defendants, who had previous criminal records, subjected the woman to such prolonged and severe abuse and starvation that they must have understood that their actions could result in her death. Prosecutors therefore consider the circumstances to constitute particular cruelty.

They have asked the appeals court to convict the male defendant of murder committed with particular cruelty and sentence him to life imprisonment. They are also seeking a substantially longer sentence for his wife.

The case will now be decided by the Debrecen Court of Appeal.

World.title: Autumn around the corner? Cold front to bring strong winds and storms to Hungary this weekend!
World.content:
Temperatures will remain summer-like in many parts of the country, but a cold front arriving on Saturday will bring stronger winds, scattered showers and thunderstorms.

Hungary is set for a changeable start to September, with a cold front bringing strong winds and scattered showers and thunderstorms on Saturday.

According to the latest forecast from HungaroMet, temperatures will drop by a few degrees behind the front, but the country will largely retain its summer-like warmth. Sunny and mostly dry weather is expected to return on Sunday.

Friday: Warm with plenty of sunshine

Friday will remain largely sunny across Hungary, although cloud cover will temporarily increase in the east and northeast. No significant rainfall is expected, although light drizzle cannot be ruled out in a few places.

Westerly winds will pick up, with some stronger gusts possible. Temperatures will reach 27–33°C during the warmest part of the day.

Stay up-to-date with our Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Saturday: Cold front brings strong winds

Saturday will begin with plenty of sunshine, but cloud cover will increase considerably from the north during the day as a cold front moves across the country. Scattered rain and showers may develop, with isolated thunderstorms also possible, particularly in northern parts of Hungary. Most areas, however, are expected to remain dry.

The wind will undergo a noticeable change, shifting from southwesterly to northerly and northwesterly. It will strengthen across large parts of the country, with strong and locally gale-force gusts possible.

Despite the approaching front, temperatures will remain high. Morning lows will generally range between 15 and 20°C, while afternoon highs will mostly reach 26–32°C. It could be a few degrees warmer in southeastern Hungary.

If you missed it: Cold front to sweep across Hungary as September begins: but summer is not over yet

Sunday: Sunshine returns

By Sunday, the weather will settle down again. Mostly clear or slightly cloudy skies are expected, with no significant rainfall forecast anywhere in the country. Northwesterly and northerly winds will remain noticeable, occasionally becoming strong.

Temperatures will fall further overnight, with lows generally between 10 and 18°C. In sheltered locations, temperatures could dip slightly below 10°C. Afternoon temperatures are expected to reach 24–29°C, bringing a somewhat cooler but still pleasantly warm end to the weekend.

Weekend weather at a glance

🌤️ Friday: Mostly sunny, 27–33°C

Mostly sunny, 27–33°C 🌬️ Saturday: Cold front, strong to locally gale-force winds, scattered showers and thunderstorms, 26–32°C

Cold front, strong to locally gale-force winds, scattered showers and thunderstorms, 26–32°C ☀️ Sunday: Mostly sunny and dry, 24–29°C

While the cold front will briefly ease the summer heat, autumn-like weather is not yet taking over Hungary. Summer warmth is expected to remain the dominant feature as September gets underway.

World.title: FM Anita Orbán shares what Hungary expects from Ukraine in order for the government to withdraw its veto
World.content:
Hungary has once again blocked progress in Ukraine’s EU accession talks, saying it is waiting for Kyiv to implement an agreement on the rights of the Hungarian minority in Ukraine.

Budapest did not approve the screening reports for the second and third negotiating clusters, preventing the accession process from moving forward on those areas.

According to the Hungarian News Agency (MTI), Hungarian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said on Thursday that the government’s position on Ukraine’s EU membership remained firm and that Hungary would not support an accelerated accession process “under any circumstances”.

Budapest wants Ukraine to implement June agreement

Speaking at the opening of the Conference on Cultural Diplomacy, Orbán said Hungary’s expectations were clearly linked to an agreement reached between the two countries in June concerning the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia.

Under the agreement, Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, is expected to adopt legislative amendments guaranteeing minority rights in areas including education, culture and political representation.

The deadline for implementing the education-related commitments is 31 December 2026, while measures concerning other areas, including political participation, are expected to be adopted in 2027.

“What we expect is the implementation of the minority agreement negotiated in June,” Orbán said. This means that the Rada must adopt the legislative amendments needed to guarantee the rights agreed upon by the two countries in the fields of education, culture and political representation.

According to Hungarian government information, Ukraine’s government has already prepared the necessary draft legislation. The proposals are currently being circulated between ministries before potentially being submitted to parliament.

Péter Magyar and Volodimir Zelensky at the EU Summit on 18 June 2026. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

Stay up-to-date with our Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Hungary says its position on EU membership is unchanged

Orbán stressed that Hungary does not support speeding up Ukraine’s EU accession process. She also reiterated the government’s earlier commitment to hold a referendum on Ukraine’s EU membership once Kyiv has completed the accession negotiations.

According to the minister, this position was also made clear during a recent working dinner with European Council President António Costa. Hungary’s latest move means that progress in Ukraine’s accession negotiations remains closely tied to the implementation of the bilateral minority-rights agreement.

A long-running source of tension

Relations between Hungary and Ukraine deteriorated significantly under the previous Hungarian government, with Ukraine’s war with Russia and its potential EU membership becoming major political issues in Hungary.

The previous government repeatedly raised concerns over the rights of the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia and at times used its position within EU decision-making to slow or block measures concerning Ukraine.

After Péter Magyar’s government took office, Budapest and Kyiv began negotiations aimed at improving bilateral relations. In June, the two sides reached an agreement under which Hungary agreed to withdraw its objection to the opening of the first negotiating cluster of Ukraine’s EU accession talks, provided that Ukraine addressed the rights of the Hungarian minority.

The latest dispute concerns the second and third clusters. Hungary’s current position is that it expects Kyiv to deliver on the commitments it made in June before Budapest agrees to further progress.

If you missed it: Tisza lead shrinks as Fidesz gains ground in new poll – Magyar’s ratings also slide

The deadlines are approaching

The first major deadline under the minority agreement is now only a few months away, with Ukraine expected to implement the education-related measures by the end of 2026. Other commitments, including those concerning political participation, are due to be addressed during 2027.

The Hungarian government says it is now waiting for Ukraine to turn the agreed commitments into legislation. If the necessary legal changes are not adopted within the agreed timeframe, the implementation of the first negotiating cluster would automatically be halted under the terms of the agreement.

World.title: BREAKING: Erasmus returns to Hungary – Hungarian university students can once again study abroad!
World.content:
Hungarian university students will once again be able to participate fully in the EU’s Erasmus+ programme from the 2026/2027 academic year, the government has announced. The move comes after years of dispute between Budapest and Brussels over the governance of Hungary’s university foundations.

Hungarian students are set to regain access to the European Union’s Erasmus+ exchange programme from the 2026/2027 academic year, according to an announcement by the Hungarian government on Thursday. At the same time, universities and researchers previously affected by the restrictions are expected to regain access to Horizon Europe, the EU’s flagship research and innovation programme.

The government described the development as a major achievement of the new administration’s first 100 days, saying negotiations with Brussels and the restructuring of Hungary’s university foundation system had paved the way for the return.

“The new government’s first 100 days have resulted in restoring Hungarian university students’ opportunity for European learning, gaining experience and building connections,” the government said.

Why was Hungary excluded from Erasmus?

The dispute dates back to Hungary’s university model change between 2019 and 2021. During this process, many formerly state-run universities were transferred to public-interest asset management foundations, known as KEKVA foundations.

These foundations received substantial state assets and were placed under boards of trustees, several of whose members were politicians, government officials or other figures closely linked to the executive branch. The European Commission raised concerns over potential conflicts of interest, the length of trustees’ mandates and the rules governing their appointment and dismissal.

In December 2022, EU member states therefore decided, under the bloc’s conditionality mechanism for protecting the EU budget, that new financial commitments could not be made with Hungary’s public-interest asset management foundations or the institutions they maintained.

This did not mean that Hungary as a whole was excluded from Erasmus+. Instead, the restrictions affected universities operating under the KEKVA system. In total, 21 higher-education institutions were affected, including some of Hungary’s largest universities. Around 200,000 students were impacted as EU-funded mobility opportunities gradually became unavailable to them.

Hungary launched its own alternative

The previous government responded by launching the Pannónia Scholarship Programme in 2024, financed from the Hungarian state budget. With an initial annual budget of around HUF 10 billion, the programme was designed to support thousands of Hungarian students, academics and researchers undertaking study or research trips abroad.

Pannónia also established partnerships outside Europe, but it could not fully replace Erasmus+.

The EU programme offers more than scholarships: it provides a long-established network of institutional partnerships, common rules, credit recognition arrangements and cooperation between thousands of European universities.

University reforms paved the way for Erasmus to return

After taking office, the Tisza government submitted legislation aimed at restructuring the public-interest asset management foundation system. According to the Ministry of Education and Children’s Affairs, the reforms are intended to address conflicts of interest, improve transparency and strengthen university autonomy.

Education and Children’s Affairs Minister Judit Lannert subsequently held talks with university rectors and other higher-education leaders about changing the existing foundation structure and, in some cases, phasing out the KEKVA model. The central question was how to bring the system into line with EU conflict-of-interest requirements while protecting universities’ operations and funding.

The government’s latest announcement represents the first tangible result of that process. However, the practical return to Erasmus+ may not happen simultaneously at every institution. Universities still need to renew or reactivate international partnership agreements, launch student application procedures and arrange the payment of scholarships.

World.title: Another Budapest district could tighten Airbnb rules as short-term rentals face growing restrictions
World.content:
Another Budapest district could introduce stricter rules for Airbnb and other short-term rentals, as the 13th District prepares to develop its own regulations for the sector.

The district currently has around 1,100–1,200 properties being used as private accommodation, according to Mayor József Tóth. That represents less than 5 per cent of the district’s more than 85,000 homes, meaning short-term rentals are not yet widespread enough to justify restrictions on their own.

However, the local council is concerned that tighter rules in neighbouring districts could lead to a surge in short-term rentals in the 13th District. It therefore wants to establish its own framework before such a shift takes place.

Neighbouring restrictions could push Airbnb towards the 13th District

Speaking to local TV channel TV13, Mayor József Tóth said the district needed to address the issue because a nationwide moratorium on establishing new short-term accommodation is due to expire at the end of 2026. Several Budapest districts have already introduced restrictions on short-term rentals, prompting concerns about a possible knock-on effect.

“We need to deal with this. At the end of 2026, the moratorium on establishing new short-term accommodation will expire. Meanwhile, several neighbouring districts have already regulated this area,” Tóth said. “We do not want this to have a cumulative effect and for the activity to move into the 13th District,” he added.

The mayor stressed that the current number of short-term rentals does not, in itself, warrant restrictions in the district. According to the council’s estimates, around 1,100–1,200 homes are currently used as private accommodation. Even allowing for properties that may not have been identified, the figure remains below the 5 per cent threshold that experts often consider a point at which regulation becomes particularly justified.

Complaints focus on noise and disturbances

The debate over short-term rentals is not only about the number of Airbnb properties, but also about their impact on residents and apartment buildings. Tóth said the district had received complaints concerning the use of individual properties, particularly noise and disturbances.

“There have been complaints about inappropriate use of properties. Noise and loud behaviour were particularly common, but residents are also disturbed by the fact that the lifestyle of short-term visitors often does not fit in with the usual routines of a residential building,” the mayor said.

At the same time, apartment buildings and housing cooperatives already have certain powers to regulate how individual properties can be used. Their founding documents or organisational and operational rules can contain provisions concerning short-term accommodation. The district council has also examined how other parts of Budapest — including the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th districts — have approached the issue.

Have you heard? Another Budapest city centre district may ban Airbnb – referendum on the horizon

No final ban or restriction has been decided yet

The 13th District is not currently preparing to impose a blanket ban on Airbnb. Instead, officials plan to draw up a proposal containing several possible regulatory options. Tóth pointed out that district councils do not issue the permits required for short-term accommodation themselves.

“We do not issue the permits; that is not the responsibility of the district council. In terms of use, however, we can establish a uniform set of conditions applying to apartment buildings and to the district as a whole,” he explained.

The council therefore appears to be considering a framework governing how short-term accommodation can operate rather than simply deciding whether it should be allowed or banned.

Stay up-to-date with our Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Residents will have a say

Once the proposal has been prepared, it will be opened up for public consultation. Residents, condominium representatives and relevant professionals will all have an opportunity to comment on the planned rules before they are submitted to the district council for a final decision.

“We want to make this a public process. We will display the proposal and publish it on our electronic platforms, where people will be able to comment on it,” Tóth said.

The mayor added that the council would follow the same approach it uses for other developments affecting the entire district: feedback would be taken into account before the final proposal is presented to the elected representatives.

World.title: Tisza lead shrinks as Fidesz gains ground in new poll – Magyar’s ratings also slide
World.content:
Publicus polling shows Péter Magyar’s lead over Viktor Orbán on suitability for the premiership narrowing, although the Tisza leader and current prime minister remains significantly ahead.

Support for Hungary’s Fidesz party increased slightly in August while backing for the ruling Tisza Party fell, according to a new poll by the Publicus Institute commissioned by daily Népszava.

The survey also found that fewer Hungarians now consider Péter Magyar suitable to serve as prime minister, while Viktor Orbán’s rating on the same question improved. Despite the shift, Magyar remains considerably more popular than Orbán among the overall population.

The poll was conducted between 18 and 25 August, with 1,006 people interviewed by telephone. Data collection was completed before the controversy surrounding the appointment of the head of Hungary’s Asset Recovery Office.

Tisza still holds a commanding lead among decided voters

Among voters who have decided which party they would support, 65 per cent backed Tisza, while 24 per cent supported Fidesz. Tisza’s support fell by three percentage points compared with July, while Fidesz gained one point. Despite the movement, the governing party still holds a substantial 41-percentage-point lead among certain party voters.

The smaller parties remained well behind the two main contenders. Mi Hazánk and the Hungarian Two-Tailed Dog Party each stood at around 1 per cent among decided voters.

Looking at the entire sample, Tisza was supported by 48 per cent of respondents, compared with 19 per cent for Fidesz. Mi Hazánk received 5 per cent, while the Democratic Coalition and Two-Tailed Dog Party each registered 1 per cent. Meanwhile, 26 per cent of respondents were uncertain about which party they would support, three percentage points more than a month earlier.

Márk Radnai and Péter Magyar. Photo: Facebook/Radnai Márk

Hungarians slightly less satisfied with the direction of the country

The poll also detected a modest deterioration in public satisfaction with the way things are going in Hungary. In late August, 61 per cent of respondents said they were rather satisfied with the country’s direction, down two percentage points from July. The proportion who were dissatisfied increased by four points.

There was a sharp partisan divide in the responses. Around 91 per cent of Tisza voters said they were satisfied, compared with just 9 per cent of Fidesz supporters. Among undecided voters, 49 per cent were satisfied with the direction of the country, while 42 per cent were dissatisfied.

Magyar remains ahead of Orbán, but the gap is narrowing

The survey also asked respondents whether they considered Péter Magyar and Viktor Orbán suitable to serve as Hungary’s prime minister.

Magyar was considered rather suitable by 57 per cent, while 34 per cent considered him rather unsuitable. His rating has nevertheless deteriorated significantly: in July, the figures stood at 62 per cent to 30 per cent, while an earlier Publicus poll recorded a 72–21 split.

Orbán, meanwhile, saw his rating improve. Thirty-three per cent of respondents considered the former prime minister rather suitable to lead the country, while 61 per cent considered him unsuitable. In July, the figures were 29 per cent and 65 per cent respectively.

This means Magyar’s advantage over Orbán on the suitability question has narrowed from 33 percentage points in July to 24 points in August.

Stay up-to-date with our Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Sharp divide between the two political camps

The partisan divide remains particularly pronounced. Among Tisza supporters, 97 per cent considered Magyar suitable for the post of prime minister, while only 3 per cent of Fidesz voters agreed. Conversely, 93 per cent of Fidesz voters considered Orbán suitable to lead the country, compared with just 4 per cent among Tisza supporters.

Among undecided voters, Orbán had a slight advantage: 41 per cent considered him suitable for the premiership, compared with 33 per cent for Magyar.

The Publicus survey was conducted for Népszava between 18 and 25 August among a representative sample of 1,006 people by telephone. As the fieldwork ended before the appointment of the head of the Asset Recovery Office, the poll does not capture any potential impact of that subsequent political controversy.

World.title: Orbán’s son named as head of Chad medical mission in non-public government resolution
World.content:
Newly obtained documents suggest Gáspár Orbán had a far more prominent role in Hungary’s controversial Chad mission than previously acknowledged.

Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s son, Gáspár Orbán, was named as the person responsible for leading a Hungarian medical mission to Chad in a non-public government resolution, according to official documents obtained by Hungarian news outlet 444.hu.

The documents shed new light on the role played by the former prime minister’s son in Hungary’s planned African mission, suggesting that his responsibilities went considerably beyond simply participating in preparations.

According to 444.hu, the documents include non-public government resolutions and records connected to the mission. They reportedly show that Gáspár Orbán was placed in a position of authority over both military personnel and the medical mission’s coordinator.

Gáspár Orbán named as head of medical mission

A medical mission travelled to Chad between 21 September and 5 October 2023. A non-public government resolution concerning the mission reportedly identified Gáspár Orbán as the person responsible for leading the entire medical mission.

The document placed both the military leadership and the medical mission coordinator under his authority. The Hungarian consul was reportedly the only person at the same level in the organisational structure, although no other officials were assigned under the consul.

The documents also point to Gáspár Orbán having played a leading role in an earlier mission to Niger.

One document reportedly states that Hungary Helps and the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences acted according to instructions issued by the Coordination Office, headed by “Gáspár O.”

Niger mission later became Chad operation

The original plans reportedly focused on Niger, but political developments in the West African country prompted Hungary to change the destination.

Chad subsequently became the focus of the project, which was broader than a military operation. According to Telex, when then-Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó announced the initiative in December 2023, he described it as involving security, economic, humanitarian and educational cooperation.

Documents obtained by 444.hu reportedly show that Gáspár Orbán was a member of the Africa Working Group (MUCS) established in connection with the Chad mission.

However, the documents suggest his involvement went significantly beyond ordinary membership. According to 444.hu’s reporting, several internal documents indicate that activities connected to the project required his approval.

Stay up-to-date with our Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Government officials gave conflicting accounts

The newly reported documents appear to contrast with earlier statements from Hungarian government and military officials about Gáspár Orbán’s involvement.

In April, then-Chief of Staff Gábor Böröndi confirmed that the former prime minister’s son had participated in the government planning group dealing with the Chad mission. At the same time, however, Böröndi described claims that Gáspár Orbán had led the group as a “gross exaggeration”.

“We had a dedicated planning team in place, which was led by my deputy, Lieutenant General Ferenc Kajári,” Böröndi said at the time.

Former government minister Gergely Gulyás had previously claimed that Gáspár Orbán had played no role in preparing the Chad mission.

However, former Defence Minister Kristóf Szalay-Bobrovniczky had given a different account. In both an interview and a 2024 parliamentary hearing, he said Gáspár Orbán had been involved in preparing the mission after being assigned to the ministerial cabinet.

Orbán’s son had already been linked to the secret mission

Gáspár Orbán’s involvement in the African operation first attracted widespread attention in early 2024, when investigative outlet Direkt36 reported on his role. The outlet published photographs and videos appearing to show him personally taking part in negotiations involving the Hungarian delegation in Chad.

More recently, Army Captain Szilveszter Pálinkás told Telex that Gáspár Orbán had been given an office in the Karmelita complex in Budapest after graduating from the Royal Military Academy in the United Kingdom, where he held the rank of first lieutenant. According to Pálinkás, he subsequently began working on the planning of the African mission.

World.title: The European Union strengthens FDI screening
World.content:
Expert Corner

Regulation (EU) 2026/1386 on the screening of foreign direct investments (FDI), in force since 16 July 2026, repeals Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and reshapes the EU screening framework. It provides for an 18-month transitional period in which Member States must adapt their legislation and administrative mechanisms. Certain provisions, including those on notification of national measures, the common information form, the secure European information-exchange infrastructure and the Commission's delegated powers, are already in force since 16 July 2026.

A mandatory screening framework and a broader concept of foreign investment



The main change is the obligation for every Member State to establish and maintain a national foreign investment screening mechanism. Extending this obligation across the EU strengthens oversight and closes the gaps that allowed certain problematic foreign investors to use Member States without screening mechanisms as gateways to the internal market for investments in sensitive assets.

A common minimum scope of strategic sectors



The Regulation introduces a mandatory minimum scope for prior authorisation. It covers Union undertakings involved in dual-use items, military equipment and sensitive technologies, including semiconductors, quantum technologies and certain artificial-intelligence technologies. The scope also extends to critical energy, transport and digital infrastructure identified through a national risk-based assessment; activities relating to strategic raw materials; and systemically important financial entities, such as central counterparties, central securities depositories, regulated-market and payment-system operators and specialised financial-messaging providers.



Electoral infrastructure is expressly included. Investments in entities that own, develop or operate voter-registration databases, voting systems or other IT systems used to manage electoral operations must be subject to prior authorisation. This reflects the Union's concern with foreign influence, access to sensitive data and technological vulnerabilities affecting democratic processes.

Prior authorisation, ex post review and coordinated procedures



Investments falling within the mandatory scope must be notified and reviewed before completion. National procedures must include at least two phases. The initial review must be completed within 45 calendar days from the date on which the filing is deemed complete. Where necessary, an in-depth investigation should be carried out, while its detailed procedural framework remains largely at the discretion of each Member State.



The Regulation also reinforces ex post control. Investments falling within the scope of a Member State's screening mechanism but which are not subject to prior authorisation may be examined on the authority's own initiative from at least 15 months and up to five years after completion, if there are reasons to consider that such an investment may affect security or public order. Investments that should have been authorised but were not notified, or were notified only after completion, must remain reviewable for at least 24 months after completion.



For transactions requiring filings in several Member States, applications must be submitted on the same day and must identify the parallel filings. The authorities concerned must coordinate their procedures and seek to align decision timetables, a point of direct relevance to cross-border M&A transactions.

Stronger EU cooperation and procedural safeguards



Member States must notify the Commission and the other Member States of specified investments, including cases involving the common minimum scope and investors controlled by third-country governments, subject to EU restrictive measures, or previously involved in prohibited investments or in breaches of mitigation measures. Notification is also required when an in-depth investigation is opened and the target participates in a project or programme of Union interest or belongs to a group operating in several Member States.



The Commission and other Member States may issue reasoned opinions or comments and the Commission may recommend mitigation measures, although the final decision remains with the screening Member State. Information requirements will be standardised and will cover the investor, beneficial owner, ownership structure, financing and source of funds, planned completion, group structure and links with projects or programmes of Union interest. Exchanges will take place through a secure, encrypted European system. At the request of at least nine Member States, the Commission will also establish an online Union filing portal.



Investors benefit from minimum procedural safeguards. Screening rules must be transparent and non-discriminatory, affected parties must have access to an effective judicial remedy, and they must be given an opportunity to express their views before an investment is prohibited, unwound or authorised subject to mitigation measures.

Romania: an existing mechanism that requires targeted alignment



Romania already operates a national FDI screening mechanism under GEO No. 46/2022, as amended. It provides for the prior authorisation of investments made by foreign investors and, in certain cases, EU investors. The applicable threshold is EUR 5 million, although lower-value investments may also be screened if they are capable of affecting national security, public order or projects and programmes of Union interest. Similar or interdependent transactions carried out within one year between the same parties and concerning the same undertaking may be treated as a single investment. Interdependent transactions individually valued below EUR 5 million must be aggregated, and the notification obligation arises when their cumulative value reaches that threshold.



GEO No. 17/2026 extended the mechanism to asset deals, covering acquisitions of tangible or intangible assets in sensitive sectors as well as acquisitions of shares or equity interests. Romanian legislation already covers many sectors included in the new EU minimum scope: critical and advanced technologies, critical infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, defence, agri-food, artificial intelligence, robotics, semiconductors, cybersecurity, quantum and nuclear technologies, biotechnology, energy, transport, healthcare, communications, data processing and storage, and electoral and financial infrastructure. Targeted amendments will nevertheless be required, notably for strategic raw materials and certain critical financial infrastructures.



The Romanian mechanism also provides for ex post review, conditional authorisation and structural or behavioural measures. Where an investment was completed without the required authorisation and affects national security or public order, the Commission for the Examination of Foreign Direct Investments (CEISD) may propose measures designed to restore the previous situation. It may also recommend authorisation subject to commitments. These features are broadly consistent with the new Regulation's approach to non-notified investments and mitigation measures.



Under the current national procedure, CEISD may authorise an investment, authorise it subject to conditions or recommend rejection. Complex cases may undergo an in-depth investigation lasting 90 calendar days, extendable once by up to 45 days; the Supreme Council of National Defence may also be consulted. Romania's planned digital filing application will need to interoperate with the secure EU exchange system, European database and any online Union portal.



In practice, Romania's framework already contains much of the architecture required by Regulation (EU) 2026/1386. The main task will be precise legislative alignment: completing the sectoral scope, coordinating national and EU digital systems, adapting deadlines and notification flows, and managing the interaction between FDI screening and merger control from the transaction-structuring stage.



By Cristina Bojica, Partner, Gruia Dufaut & Asociatii



*This is an expert corner.

World.title: European Council president Antonio Costa condemns violations of Romanian airspace by drones
World.content:
European Council president Antonio Costa said on Thursday, September 3, after a meeting with Romanian president Nicuşor Dan in Bucharest, that the latest violations of Romania’s airspace, as well as incidents involving maritime drones, are deeply concerning.

Costa noted that Romania’s security also means Europe’s security, while collective security is closely linked to the security of the eastern border, including the Black Sea.

“We will continue to stand firmly with Romania, because we understand that the security of Romania is Europe’s security as well. Our unity in supporting Ukraine will not be broken by Russia's attempts to intimidate us or divide us. Here, let me commend Romania’s steadfast support for Ukraine. We must continue to work united for a just and lasting peace,” Costa said, according to the official press release.

The European Council president added that he was grateful for Romania’s support for the Republic of Moldova, as well as for the assistance provided to Ukraine.

“Each enlargement has made Europe stronger politically and economically. It is one of Europe’s most important geopolitical investments. It is an investment in our security, stability and prosperity. What applied to enlargements in the past also applies to the Western Balkans, Ukraine and, of course, Moldova,” Antonio Costa further said.

According to president Nicuşor Dan, Costa is touring European capitals in preparation for the European Council in October. The main subject of the Council, he added, will be the negotiation of the European Union’s future 2028-2034 budget.

“We had an in-depth discussion, especially on this subject. Romania has defined a large part of its position within the position of the Friends of Cohesion group,” he said, referencing the 17 European states that oppose cuts to the EU’s Cohesion Policy fund.

“We want an ambitious European Union budget. We want substantial amounts for the cohesion chapter and the agriculture chapter, precisely to close the gaps between citizens of different European countries. We are very interested in the competitiveness pillar. Here again, we are talking about reducing, or targeting a reduction in, the gap between European countries, and we want companies from less developed European countries, such as Romania, to be able to access competitiveness funds,” president Dan said.

The Romanian head of state noted that compromises must be made regarding the EU budget. “We also discussed, in preparation for the October Council, the European Union enlargement process and, of course, our interest in ensuring that the accession process of the Republic of Moldova continues at a sustained pace,” Nicuşor Dan further said.

World.title: Central Romania: British TV producer Charlie Ottley to restore visitor center in village of Şirnea
World.content:
British television producer Charlie Ottley, who moved permanently to Romania and obtained Romanian citizenship at the end of last year, announced on Thursday, September 3, that he plans to restore the original visitor center in Şirnea, Braşov County, using traditional materials.

The center will become the first English pub and the first guesthouse in a Romanian village, according to the same source.

“We have big news. We are restoring with traditional materials the original visitor centre for Sirnea from back when it was the first touristic village in Romania. It was weeks from total collapse when we bought it. It is now safe and rising from the ruins to become the first English pub and guest house in a Romanian village,” Charley Ottley announced on Facebook.

The guesthouse will be called “Kings Arms” and will be dedicated to “His Majesty King Charles III, for all the love, devotion and support” he has given to “our wonderful country.”

“We look forward to being able to welcome guests in the spring,” Ottley said.

Ottley moved permanently to Romania, to the village of Şirnea, Braşov County, where he bought and completely renovated a traditional farmhouse, where he lives with his partner.

The producer of the documentaries “Wild Carpathia” and “Flavours of Romania” officially became a Romanian citizen at the end of 2025, after a five-year wait. He continues to actively promote Romanian tourism and traditions internationally through his new projects and is directly involved in preserving rural communities in the Braşov area.

(Photo source: Charlie Ottley on Facebook)

World.title: Romania’s new medical eSănătateaMea platform facing access problems, government promises fix
World.content:
The Romanian government announced that it has increased the number of staff handling account validations on the e-Sănătatea mea platform, the country’s new medical platform intended to serve as the central point of interactions between patients and the healthcare system.

In the first days since the platform was brought online, on September 1, users who tried to log in encountered serious operational problems, right from the first steps of accessing the platform. Several others reported that the platform was inaccessible.

To fix the issues, the executive increased the team of experts validating the digital identities of patients. “At present, approximately 25,000 requests for validation of digital identities are pending, amid an average flow of approximately 10,000 new requests per day. To rapidly reduce the backlog, the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania currently has 40 people trained for validation,” the government said in a press release.

The government promised that the problem will be resolved within a week, following the temporary addition of 19 staff members. Previously, 40 people were responsible for this task. “The validation process involves rigorous checks to prevent attempts at fraud, impersonation or alteration of identity,” the government further said.

The government also recommended that users install the latest version of the platform, while other enrollment solutions have already been identified for optimal operation and are to be implemented.

The new portal, integrated into the IT Platform of the Social Health Insurance System, is administered by Romania's National Health Insurance House (CNAS). The development of the portal aims to simplify the circulation of medical documents, reduce administrative burdens, and facilitate patients' access to the information they need. Through the platform, insured persons will be able to securely consult data and documents recorded in the public health insurance system.

Importantly, registration with “eSănătateaMea” will not be mandatory. People who do not use a smartphone, do not have internet access, or do not wish to use the portal will continue to be able to interact with the healthcare system through the usual procedures, according to CNAS management.

The “eSănătateaMea” is also designed to work in sync with the new electronic identity card. The latter will serve as the national social health insurance card, replacing it in the end.
